貓頭鷹（英文欽定版為“大貓頭鷹”）。可能是朱鷺或埃及鴞。

23.en: All other flying creeping things. That is, winged insects other than those specifically named. The fact that many insects carry disease accounts for the scrupulous care to be taken after coming in contact with them (vs. 23–25).
23.zh:
但是有翅膀有四足的爬物，你們都當以為可憎。

就是上述昆蟲以外的有翅膀的昆蟲。許多昆蟲都攜帶病菌，所以要小心接觸（第23-25節）。

14.en: The kite. A bird of prey belonging to the falcon family, having pointed wings and a long forked tail. After his kind. This expression indicates all members of basic types, of each of which but one is named (see vs. 15, 16, 22).
14.zh:
鷂鷹、小鷹與其類；

**小鷹。**有譯本為“鳶”，是隼科的食肉鳥，有尖尖的翅膀和分叉的尾巴。
**與其類。**表示它所屬種類的所有成員（見第15,16,22節）。

7.en: The swine. Of all animals prohibited by law, the swine was considered the most unclean (see Isa. 65:3, 4; 66:17). This is not the place to discuss at length the harm of eating swine’s flesh. For the Christian it is sufficient to stress God’s attitude toward it. There must be something unwholesome about the use of swine’s flesh, or God would not speak as He does. He created the swine and knows what they are. He prohibits their use as food. Christ did not think highly of swine or He would not have permitted the destruction of some 2,000 of them (Matt. 8:31, 32; Mark 5:13). We do not know the monetary value of those swine. Today they would bring a considerable sum of money, and no doubt represented a large investment then. Two men had been restored in mind and body, but at the cost of 2,000 swine. Christ considered the men worth it; the people thought otherwise. Whatever men may think of swine’s flesh as an acceptable article of diet, God here disapproves of it. God does not change His mind (Mal. 3:6); and it is certain that swine have not changed their nature. We do well to heed His counsel.
7.zh:
豬─因為蹄分兩瓣，卻不倒嚼，就與你們不潔淨。

在律法所禁止的動物中，豬是被視為最不潔淨的（見賽65:3,4；66:17）。本文並不是詳細討論吃豬肉的害處。就基督徒而言，強調上帝對它的態度就夠了。吃豬肉肯定有害健康，否則上帝就不會禁止了。祂創造了豬，並且知道它們的本性。祂禁止把它們當作食物。
基督並不賞識豬，否則祂就不會讓兩千多頭豬毀滅了（太8:31,32；可5:13）。我們不知道那些豬的價值。在今天，它們肯定很值錢，所以當時也代表大筆的資金。兩個人在身心上得到了康復，其代價卻是兩千頭豬。基督認為這值得；百姓卻不這樣認為。
不管人覺得豬肉如何好吃，上帝在這裡不予以認可。上帝不會改變祂的看法（瑪3:6）；豬也肯定不會改變本性。我們最好聽祂的話。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–8節）**。《論飲食》30，392；《健康勉言》116；《證言》卷一206；《證言》卷二96。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–8節）**。《論飲食》30，392；《健康勉言》116；《證言》卷一206；《證言》卷二96。

11.3: Civil. These laws applied the broad principles of the Ten Commandments to the economy of ancient Israel as a nation. Though this code became inoperative when ancient Israel ceased to be a nation and has not been reinstated as such in the modern, nontheocratic state of Israel, yet the fundamental principles of justice and equity involved are still valid.

18.en: The swan. Possibly the glossy ibis or the water hen. The ASV gives it as “horned owl.” The gier eagle. Most likely the Egyptian vulture, a bird of unclean and disgusting habits.
18.zh:
角鴟、鵜鶘、禿鵰、

**角鴟（英文KJV版為“天鵝”）。**可能是鷭或水雞。
**禿雕。**可能是埃及禿鷲，一種不潔且令人厭惡的鳥。

2.en: These are the beasts. The principles set forth in this chapter were designed of God to protect those who love and choose to serve Him against the use, as food, of those forms of animal life that would bring injury to their bodies. In a number of instances, as will be seen, it is not yet possible to identify the animals named. Where doubt exists, that fact is noted. This measure of uncertainty, however, will not prove to be an insurmountable problem to any Christian who purposes in his heart not to “defile the temple of God” (1 Cor. 3:17) but to “do all to the glory of God” (1 Cor. 10:31). For such a person the fundamental principles as outlined here will prove to be a sufficient guide. 2. Ceremonial. These laws were concerned with a system of worship that prefigured the cross, and accordingly expired at that time (Col. 2:14–17; Heb. 7:12).
2.zh:
你們曉諭以色列人說，在地上一切走獸中可吃的乃是這些：

本章所倡導的原則是上帝用來保護愛祂並選擇事奉祂的人免於食用那些會給他們的身體帶來損害的動物。下文所提到的動物，有些尚未得到確認。雖然存在疑問，但事實卻是顯而易見的。對於立志不“毀壞上帝的殿”（林前3:17），凡事“都要為榮耀上帝而行”（林前10:31）的基督徒來說，這種不確定性並不是不可克服的難題。就他們而言，這裡所概括的基本原則足以作為他的指導。

1.zh:
耶和華對摩西、亞倫說：

**懷愛倫註釋（1–8節）**。《歷代願望》617。

29.zh:
地上爬物與你們不潔淨的乃是這些：鼬鼠、鼫鼠、蜥蜴與其類；

**爬物。**包括爬行動物，齧齒動物等。
**鼬鼠。**原文指會滑行的動物。
**鼫鼠。**就是老鼠，無疑也包括其他小的齧齒動物。
蜥蜴（英文欽定版為“龜”）。指大蜥蜴，也有可能是“陸棲鱷魚”（七十士譯本），通常有兩英尺長。阿拉伯人至今仍用它的肉做湯。在其他國家，蜥蜴肉被曬乾當作飾物或藥物。

30.zh:
壁虎、龍子、守宮、蛇醫、蝘蜓。

壁虎（英文欽定版為“雪貂”）。該詞原文在《舊約》中只出現在這裡。它會發出一種哀鳴，腳趾上有吸盤，可以附吸在垂直的表面上。
龍子（英文欽定版為“變色龍”）。原文指“強壯者”。有人認為是指青蛙，因為它在跳躍時顯示了強大的肌肉力量。也有人認為是指陸棲鱷魚（見第29節註釋）。
守宮（英文欽定版為“蜥蜴”）。可能與大多數國家所發現的蜥蜴一樣。蜥蜴有許多種，都包括在“蜥蜴”這一通稱中。
蛇醫（英文欽定版為“蝸牛”）。很可能是一種“蜥蜴”（七十士譯本）。
蝘蜓（英文欽定版為“鼴鼠”）。譯自tinshemeth，指“蜥蜴”或“變色龍”。

39.zh:
你們可吃的走獸若是死了，有人摸他，必不潔淨到晚上；

禁止摸死屍的規定也適用於可以吃之動物的屍體。

40.zh:
有人吃那死了的走獸，必不潔淨到晚上，並要洗衣服；拿了死走獸的，必不潔淨到晚上，並要洗衣服。

暗示有人會吃自死動物的肉。律法嚴禁食用“田間被野獸撕裂牲畜的肉”（出22:31）。祭司不可吃“自死的或是被野獸撕裂的”動物（利22:8）。但仍有吃的情況發生，可能是由於不知情的經濟困難。由於吃這種肉屬儀文性的不潔，所以有了儀文性潔淨的規定。
禁止吃自死的或被野獸撕裂的動物，無疑是因為在這種情況下，血大都還留在體內，未被排出。

44.zh:
我是耶和華─你們的神；所以你們要成為聖潔，因為我是聖潔的。你們也不可在地上的爬物汙穢自己。

聖潔與飲食習慣之間顯然存在密切的聯繫。因此，聖潔包括順從上帝有關健康的律法。

900.zh:
有人認為上帝不會屈尊賜下有關人類飲食的指示。上帝為什麼在乎我們吃什麼呢？
我們可以進一步詢問：上帝為什麼要眷顧人呢？古時的詩人感嘆說：“人算什麼，你竟眷顧他？”（詩8:4）。基督回答了這個問題。祂告訴我們，上帝不僅眷顧人，而且眷顧許多價值更低的事物（路12:7）。
人是按照上帝的形象創造的。麻雀不是。人在上帝的眼中十分寶貴，比“精金還少；使人比俄斐純金”更有價值（賽13:12；43:4）。上帝對人的評價，可以從祂把自己與人視為一體中看出來。“摸你們的，就是摸他眼中的瞳人”（亞2:8）。上帝付出如此重大的代價來救贖人類，對於基督徒來說，更說明上帝所賦予他的價值。因此我們可以相信，凡與人有關的事情都是上帝所關心的。
上帝有關飲食的律法並不像一些人所認為的，只是負面和禁止性的。上帝希望人擁有最好的東西，擁有“上好的麥子”（詩81:16；147:14）。創造萬物的主知道什麼對祂所造之物最為有益，並按照祂的智慧給予勸戒和忠告。“祂未嘗留下一樣好處，不給那些行動正直的人”（詩84:11）。上帝所禁止的決不是武斷的扣留，而是為了人的益處。人可以蔑視上帝的忠告，但事實和後果總是證明祂的智慧。
上帝賜給人奇妙的身體。它擁有幾乎無限的前途。人體的許多微妙部分必須小心維護，免遭濫用，才能保持正常的運作。祂在人體內提供了照料和保養各部分的機制。只要遵循祂的指示，它們甚至能自動更新。在許多情況下，即使人體已經多年濫用，仍能開始復原的過程。自然界恢復的能力是驚人的。人體的任何部位一受到傷害，身體中的生命力立即就開始工作來修復損害。醫生可以協助做很多的好事，但他們卻沒有醫治的能力。在許多情況下，他們所能做的，就是站到一旁，讓上帝工作。
有人認為上帝關心人的靈魂超過他的身體，屬靈的價值高於身體的價值。這是對的。但要記住身體和靈魂是密切相關的，彼此能造成很大的影響，往往很難確定它們之間的界限。雖然我們認為屬靈方面是非常重要的，但我們不能因此而疏忽身體。中世紀的某些“聖徒”確實有這樣的理念。他們是為了靈魂的益處而苦修身體；但那並不是上帝的旨意。祂將身體和心靈放在一起考慮，是為了雙方相互的利益。
“心怎樣思量，他為人就是怎樣”（箴23:7）。這句話觸及了生命的基本問題。一個人怎樣想，他就會怎麼樣。思維會對身體的行為產生影響嗎？脫離了某種機制還能進行思考嗎？不論人思什麼，都會決定行為。如果一個人按正確的方式思考，他的行為可能就是正確的。如果他思考罪惡的事情，他的行為就可能是邪惡的。
身體會對人的思維產生影響嗎？肯定會的。大家都知道酒既影響人的行為，也影響人的思維。它會扭曲他的判斷力，使他不負責任。他的頭腦不能像他清醒時那樣運作。他機能不能正常地工作。他所有的反應都變得遲鈍了。如果他駕車，就會威脅他人，成為潛在的殺手（見利10:9註釋）。
大多數人都承認飲酒有不良的作用。錯誤的飲食習慣會有類似的作用嗎？會的，儘管其程度與飲酒不同。食物會影響一個人的思維，也會影響人的行為。許多孩子因父親的麵包片烤糊了，咖啡淡了或冷了而捱揍。許多人離婚的原因可以追溯到家裡的廚房。推銷員不會從消化不良的客戶那裡獲得大筆定單。精明的律師知道什麼時候可以接近法官，予以收買，獲得優惠。外交官和政治家知道盛宴的價值。如果把酒和食物巧妙地結合起來，就能簽下在正常情況下絕不會簽訂的協議。這種協議給世界帶來了幾代人詛咒。
食物會影響思維嗎？吃喝會影響心靈嗎？肯定會的。陰鬱的人生觀常常來自泛酸的胃。正確的飲食不一定產生美好的性情，但錯誤的飲食很難使人達到上帝所定的標準。
上帝關於飲食的律法並不是強行剝奪人的口福，而是合情合理的。人如果想保持健康或恢復健康，最好關注一下這些律法。總的來說，上帝所認可的食物和人所認為最好的食物是一致的。分歧不在一致認同的食物，而在所禁止的食物。
這些飲食的規定是賜給古時以色列人的，適用於他們的環境。大多數猶太人仍遵守這些法規。這些法規在三千多年的時間裡一直髮揮得很好。如果說，這些規定是為了造就能擺脫現今危害人類之諸多疾病的民族的話，猶太人的身體狀況足以證明這些規定並沒有失效或過時。儘管猶太人所遭受的逼迫和苦難比世界上任何民族都多，時間也更長，但總的說來，他們仍是強健的種族。至少其部分原因是他們遵守上帝在利11章中所設立的飲食律法。
在西奈山賜給以色列人的律法涉及他們對上帝和人類的各方面義務，可以分為以幾類：
一. 道德律法。 十誡中所表達的原則反映了上帝的品格，和上帝一樣是不可改變的（見太5:17,18；羅3:31）。
二. 儀文律法。 涉及預表十字架的敬拜體系，到主釘十字架後就過期了（西2:14-17；來7:12）。
三. 民事律法。 把十誡的廣泛原則應用在了古以色列民族的經濟體制中。儘管這部法典在古以色列人亡國以後就失效了，而且現代世俗的以色列國也沒有恢復這些制度，但其中公正與平等的基本原則依然是有效的。
四. 健康律。智慧的創造主制定利11章的飲食原則和其他衛生健康法規，是為了促進人的健康和長壽的（見出15:26；23:25；申7:15；詩105:37；《先祖與先知》第378頁）。它們是根據人體的性質和條件制定的，所以不受基督釘十字架或以色列亡國的影響。3,500年前的健康原則今天仍會產生同樣的效果。
忠心的基督徒把自己的身體看作聖靈的殿（林前3:16,17；6:19,20）。他既認識到這一點，除了其他的事情以外，他還要在吃喝上榮耀上帝，按照上帝所啟示的旨意調整自己的飲食（林前9:27；10:31）。他一定會始終不逾地接受和順服利11章所規定的原則。

27.en: One of the common people. The procedure was the same as in the case of a ruler, with the exception that the common man was to bring a female rather than a male. The female was somewhat lower in the scale of value than the male, and therefore more easily acquired. The ritual of the blood and the disposal of the fat were the same as for rulers who had sinned (vs. 23–26).
27.zh:
民中若有人行了耶和華所吩咐不可行的什麼事，誤犯了罪，

其程序與官長的情況一樣。但普通人所的是母畜而不是公畜。母畜的價值略低於公畜，因此比較容易得到。施血的儀式和脂油的處理與官長犯罪的情形一樣（第23-26節）。
**懷愛倫註釋（27–30節）**。《先祖與先知》354。
**懷愛倫註釋（27–30節）**。《先祖與先知》354。

7.en: Upon the horns of the altar. Besides sprinkling the blood before the veil, the priest also put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of incense. In doing so he touched each horn in turn, making a mark of blood with his finger, thus registering the fact that sin had been committed and that an offering had been brought. The blood that he placed on the horns was from an animal that bore sin, and hence was sin-laden blood. This necessitated that there should be made “an atonement upon the horns of it once in a year” (Ex. 30:10). The unused portion of the blood was poured out at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering.
7.zh:
又要把些血抹在會幕內、耶和華面前香壇的四角上，再把公牛所有的血倒在會幕門口、燔祭壇的腳那裡。

除了對著幔子彈血以外，祭司還把一些血抹在香壇的四角上。他逐一觸摸每一個角，用他的指頭留下血跡，表明罪已犯下，但祭已獻上。他抹在四角的血來自一隻擔罪的祭牲，因此是擔罪之血。所以需要“一年一次，要在壇的角上行贖罪之禮”（出30:10）。未用掉的血要倒在燔祭壇的腳那裡。

6.en: Sprinkle of the blood. As there was no one higher in rank than the high priest, who could officiate for him, he ministered the blood himself. In the sacrifices previously considered, the blood was sprinkled on the altar of burnt offering in the court or placed upon its horns. But when the anointed priest sinned, the blood was carried into the sanctuary itself. This was doubtless because his sin was considered more serious than that of anyone else, and of more concern to God. The priest dipped his finger in some of the blood and sprinkled it seven times before the veil, “before the Lord.” Also, he put some of the blood upon the horns of the altar of incense, which is also said to be “before the Lord” (v. 7). It should be noted that the priest did not sprinkle the blood on the veil, but before it. It is also of interest that he used only one finger in sprinkling. Furthermore, this sprinkling was done only when the anointed priest or the whole congregation sinned. We have no record of how often the high priest sinned and brought a bullock as an offering, but it was probably not often. Again, we do not know how often the whole people sinned and had to bring a bullock, but we suppose that this was not often. That the people often sinned individually is evident, but we have few records of national sins, such as are here contemplated. The only definite record we have was when they sinned and danced about the golden calf. True, there were other national apostasies, but as the offering was only to be brought when they repented of their sins, there could not have been many instances. The sprinkling took place with reference to the law, which was directly behind the veil. However, the blood did not reach the law; the veil intervened. In the daily service the time had not come for the sinner to face the law. That was reserved for the Day of Atonement, which, in type, was the day of judgment for Israel (see on Heb. 10:19, 20).
6.zh:
把指頭蘸於血中，在耶和華面前對著聖所的幔子彈血七次，

由於沒有比大祭司級別更高的人來為他供職，他只好自己處置血。在上面的祭禮中，血是灑在院子裡的燔祭壇上或抹在壇的角上。但當受膏的祭司犯罪時，血要帶進聖所中。這無疑是因為他的罪被認為比任何其他人的罪更加嚴重，而且更受上帝所關注。祭司把指頭蘸在血中並在幔子前，也就是“在耶和華面前”彈血七次。他還要把一些血抹在香壇的角上。這香壇也是被稱為在“耶和華面前”的（第7節）。
值得注意的是，祭司沒有把血彈在幔子上，而是對著幔子彈。還要注意他只用一個指頭彈血。況且這種彈血只在受膏的祭司或全會眾犯罪時才施行。聖經沒有記錄大祭司有多少次犯罪和帶公牛犢來獻祭，但這可能是不常發生的。我們也不知道全會眾有多少次犯罪而獻公牛犢，但我們估計這也不常發生的。百姓個人顯然經常犯罪。但很少有這裡所討論的全國性犯罪的記錄。唯一一次確切的記載就是他們圍著金牛犢犯罪和跳舞。當然後來還有其他全國性背道的情況。但只有他們悔改時才獻祭，所以獻這種祭並不太多。
彈血與幔子後面的律法有關。但是血沒有達到律法那裡，因為當中隔著幔子。在每日的崇事中，罪人面對律法的時候還沒有到。這要留到贖罪日。贖罪日預表以色列人審判的日子（見來10:19,20註釋）。

8.en: The fat of the bullock. See on ch. 3:3, 5. There is no mention here of its being “a sweet savour unto the Lord.” The fact that it was permitted on the altar, however, indicates that it was pleasing to God.
8.zh:
要把贖罪祭公牛所有的脂油，乃是蓋臟的脂油和臟上所有的脂油，

見利3:3,5註釋。這裡沒有說是“獻與耶和華為馨香的”。但允許放在壇上表明是上帝所悅納的。

3.en: Sin is disobedience. Disobedience is possible only where there is a knowledge of the law and transgression of it. There are different degrees of guilt in disobedience, and God provides for this. But all transgression is serious. The persistently impenitent will eventually commit the sin that is unpardonable. 3. The priest that is anointed. All priests were anointed, but the high priest only was anointed on the head; hence, by way of pre-eminence, he is here called “the priest that is anointed” (see Ex. 29:7–9; Lev. 8:12, 13). He is designated as “the high priest among his brethren, upon whose head the anointing oil was poured” (Lev. 21:10). Ordinarily he is called simply “the priest.” Only four times in the books of Moses is he called “high priest,” and in each case a literal translation would be “great priest” or “chief priest” (see Lev. 21:10; Num. 35:25, 28). According to the sin of the people. Rather, “thus bringing guilt on the people” (RSV). The high priest stood for and represented the people (see Lev. 16:15, 16; Zech. 3:1–4). In harmony with this principle the prophets always identified themselves with the sins of the people. Although as God’s messengers they rebuked the people for their transgressions, when they prayed to God they approached Him as if they were one with the people in the sins rebuked. So we find them repeatedly saying, “We have sinned,” not merely “they have sinned”; “we have sinned against the Lord”; “we have sinned against him”; “we have sinned, we have done wickedly” (Neh. 1:6; Isa. 64:5, 7; Jer. 3:25; 8:14; 14:7; Dan. 9:5, 8, 11, 15). The representative character of the high priest needs to be stressed. He was the representative man, the one who acted for the people in all things pertaining to the sanctuary. And in the high priest the whole priesthood was summed up. When Adam sinned, “death passed upon all men” (Rom. 5:12), for “by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners” (Rom. 5:19). Adam was the representative man. Christ was likewise the representative man. Adam, the “first man,” was the head of humanity; Christ, the “second man,” the “last Adam,” “the Lord from heaven,” is the head of the new humanity (1 Cor. 15:45–47). “As by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; even so by the righteousness of one the free gift came upon all men unto justification of life” and “by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous” (Rom. 5:18, 19). “For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive” (1 Cor. 15:22). The high priest, being in a special sense a figure of Christ, was the representative man. He stood for all Israel. He carried their burdens and sins. He bore the iniquity of the holy things. He bore the judgment of Israel. When he sinned, Israel sinned. When he entered the sanctuary, he went in on behalf of the people. And when he appeared before God, they appeared. He represented the people; he was the people. When he sinned, the people sinned, and he was required to bring the same sacrifice for his sin as when the whole nation sinned. A young bullock without blemish. Both male and female animals could be used in sin offerings; but they must be “without blemish.” It was a young bullock the high priest offered for his sin, as for the sin of all the people (Lev. 4:14).
3.zh:
或是受膏的祭司犯罪，使百姓陷在罪裡，就當為他所犯的罪把沒有殘疾的公牛犢獻給耶和華為贖罪祭。

**受膏的祭司。**所有的祭司都是受膏的，但只有大祭司是在頭上受膏的；所以稱他為“受膏的祭司”（見出29:7-9；利8:12,13），以示區別。他被稱為“在弟兄中作大祭司，頭上倒了膏油”的（利21:10），簡稱“祭司”，摩西的書中只有四次稱為“大祭司”（見利21:10；民35:25,28）。
**使百姓陷在罪裡。**大祭司代表百姓（見利16:15,16；亞3:1-4）。同樣，先知總是把百姓的罪說成是自己的罪。雖然他們作為上帝的使者斥責百姓的罪過，但他們向上帝禱告時，總把自己當作犯受斥責之罪的百姓中的一員來親近祂。他們常常說：“我們犯了罪”，而不只是“他們犯了罪”；“我們得罪了耶和華”；“我們得罪了上帝”；“我們犯了罪，作了惡”（尼1:6；賽64:5,7；耶3:25；8:14；14:7；但9:5,8,11,15）。
需要重視大祭司的代表性。他是人類的代表，在與聖所有關的一切事上為百姓工作。在大祭司身上，集中了整個祭司職分的功能。
亞當犯罪以後，“死就臨到眾人”（羅5:12）。“因一人的悖逆，眾人成為罪人”（羅5:19）。亞當是人類的代表。基督也是人類的代表。“首先的人”亞當是人類的頭；“第二個人”，“末後的亞當”，“出於天的”基督，是新人的頭（林前15:45-47）。“如此說來，因一次的過犯，眾人都被定罪；照樣，因一次的義行，眾人也就被稱義得生命了”。“因一人的順從，眾人也成為義了”（羅5:18,19）。“在亞當裡眾人都死了；照樣，在基督裡眾人也都要復活”（林前15:22）。
大祭司從特殊意義上說是基督的預表。他也是人類的代表，代表所有的以色列人。他擔當了他們的重擔和罪孽，承擔了他們對聖物的干犯，承受了對以色列人的懲罰。他如果犯罪，以色列人也就犯了罪。他進入聖所，是代表百姓的。他來到上帝面前，就是代表百姓來到上帝面前。他代表百姓；他就是百姓。他犯罪就是百姓犯罪，需要為他的罪獻上和全民族犯罪時一樣的祭物。
**沒有殘疾的公牛犢。**公牛的母牛都可以用於贖罪祭，但必須是“沒有殘疾的”。大祭司為自己的罪所獻的是一隻公牛犢，和為全會眾的罪所獻的一樣（利4:14）。

32.en: A lamb for a sin offering. A lamb was even less expensive than a goat, and for this reason it was expected that a poor man would bring a lamb. The lamb was therefore considered the poor man’s offering. It is significant that Christ is repeatedly spoken of as the Lamb of God. He is the poor man’s sacrifice. The ritual was in all respects the same as that for a goat. Provision for a graduated scale with regard to the value of the prescribed offerings reflects both the justice and the mercy of God. In the first place, the value of the sacrifice to be brought was determined by the degree of responsibility of the sinner, and in the second, by his ability to provide an offering.
32.zh:
人若牽一隻綿羊羔為贖罪祭的供物，必要牽一隻沒有殘疾的母羊，

**一隻綿羊羔為贖罪祭。**羊羔比山羊便宜。窮人可以獻上一隻羊羔。因此羊羔被視為窮人的祭物。值得注意的是基督一再被稱為“上帝的羔羊”。祂是窮人的祭物。儀式的各方面要求都與獻山羊一樣。
關於所指定供物價值等級的規定，反映了上帝的公義和慈愛。應獻祭物的價值首先是由罪人責任的大小來決定的，其次還要依據他提祭供物的能力。

31.en: For a sweet savour. Inasmuch as the fat was always burned on the altar it must have been acceptable to God, for nothing unclean was ever permitted on the altar.
31.zh:
又要把羊所有的脂油都取下，正如取平安祭牲的脂油一樣。祭司要在壇上焚燒，在耶和華面前作為馨香的祭，為他贖罪，他必蒙赦免。

脂油都要焚燒在壇上，所以它一定蒙上帝所悅納，因為任何不潔之物都不得獻在壇上。

12.en: Without the camp. The whole bullock was carried without the camp and burned in a clean place, not merely to dispose of it, nor because it was considered unclean, for it is distinctly called “most holy” (ch. 6:25). The book of Hebrews attaches a symbolic meaning to the burning of the victim without the camp. Says Paul, “Jesus also … suffered without the gate. Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach” (Heb. 13:12, 13). The burning of the body without the camp was then a type of Christ, crucified outside the city of Jerusalem, “that he might sanctify the people with his own blood” (Heb. 13:12). Some have seen in this the further thought that He died not for the Jews only but for the world. No sacrificial use was made of the body even though it was considered most holy. As it was not burned on the altar, no redemptive value inhered in it. It was therefore not the body that counted in the atonement, for “it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul” (Lev. 17:11). However, it was not the blood as such that atoned, but the blood shed and applied. No atonement could have been effected in the sacrificial service by having an animal killed and the blood poured out on the ground. It was to be caught in a vessel, after which the priest ministered it by sprinkling and otherwise. It was the sprinkled blood that effected atonement, not the unused portion of the blood later poured out on the ground (see on ch. 4:7). The atonement was made by the blood that was put on the horns of the altar, not by that which was poured out on the ground (Ex. 29:12; Ex. 30:10; Lev. 4:7, 18, 25, 30, 34). It is unfortunate that Christians stress the “spilt blood,” an expression not found in the Bible, and forget the “sprinkled” blood, which alone effected atonement. The spilt blood was the unused blood, that which was poured out at the bottom of the altar after the atonement was completed. Paul speaks of “the blood of sprinkling” (Heb. 12:24), that is, the blood that was ministered. At the institution of the Passover, Israel was commanded to slay a lamb and strike the blood on the lintel and on the two side posts (Ex. 12:7, 22, 23). God did not promise to save the first-born by virtue of the slaying of the lamb. It was only when the blood was applied that He would “pass over.” The same principle holds good in all offerings. It is not enough to bring a victim and slay it; the blood must be applied. After His ascension Christ “by his own blood … entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us” (Heb. 9:12), and there as a “high priest, … a minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle” (Heb. 8:1–3), He ministers on our behalf. This phase of the ministry of Christ is as necessary to our salvation as was the ministry of the blood of the lamb at the time of the first Passover, and as with all offerings in which blood was shed. The ministry of the blood on the great Day of Atonement was the high point in the yearly service. The killing of the victim was certainly important—without it there would be no blood to minister—but the climax was reached when the high priest went into the most holy with the blood of the Lord’s goat (see Heb. 9:25). Similarly, Christ “by his own blood … entered in once into the holy place” (Heb. 9:12). His death on Calvary was essential—without it He would have nothing “to offer” (Heb. 8:3)—but without the continuing ministry of the blood in the sanctuary above, the sacrifice on Calvary would be unavailing. Most Christians neither understand nor appreciate Christ’s ministry as our great High Priest. To be sure, they believe in the shed blood; but they fail to understand that there must be a ministry, or application, of the blood to make it effective. It is time that the attention of the world, and of professed Christians in particular, be called to the work in which Christ is now engaged. Many ask why Christ tarries so long. They know He went away, but they know nothing of His mediatorial work. They have not followed the Lamb, and know not where He now is and what work He is doing. It is our duty and privilege, our appointed task as a people, to restore the old paths (see Isa. 58:12), and to present Christ to the world in His mediatorial capacity as our great High Priest. His work is nearly done, and when it is finished He will come in power and glory.
12.zh:
就是全公牛，要搬到營外潔淨之地、倒灰之所，用火燒在柴上。

整頭公牛犢要帶到營外，在一個潔淨的地方燒掉，不只是為了處理它，也不是因為它被認為是不潔的，因為它已明確地稱為“是至聖的”（利6:25）。《希伯來書》賦予營外燒祭牲的做法以屬靈的解釋。保羅說：“耶穌……也就在城門外受苦。這樣，我們也當出到營外，就了他去，忍受祂所受的凌辱”（來13:12,13）。公牛在營外焚燒，預表基督在耶路撒冷城外被釘，“用自己的血叫百姓成聖”（來13:12）。有人進一步理解這是指祂不但是為猶太人而死，也是為全世界的人而死的。身體雖然被認為是至聖的，但沒有用作祭物。它沒有在壇上燒，所以它本身不具備救贖的價值。贖罪中有價值的不是身體，因為“血裡有生命，所以能贖罪”（利17:11）。
然而起贖罪作用的，並不是血本身，而是血的傾流和處置。在獻祭的崇事中，贖罪的生效靠的不是殺死祭牲、把血倒在地上。必須把血接在一個器皿裡，然後祭司要灑血或用其他方式處理。使贖罪生效的，正是這所灑的血，而不是未用掉被倒在地上的血（見利4:7註釋）。贖罪是靠抹在壇的四角上的血而實現的，而不是憑倒在地上的血（出29:12；出30:10；利4:7,18,25,30,34）。
不幸的是基督徒強調“流出的血”。這是聖經所沒有的說法。他們忘記了唯一能使贖罪生效的，是“被灑”的血。流出的血乃是未用掉的血，是在贖罪完成之後倒在壇腳下的。保羅說的“所灑的血”（來12:24），就是所施用的血。在設立逾越節時，以色列人奉命要宰殺一隻羊羔，並把血塗在門楣和兩邊的門框上（出12:7,22,23）。上帝並沒有承諾憑著宰殺羊羔的而拯救頭生的。只有血被施用時，祂才會“越過去”。
這個原則也適用於所有其他的祭物。只帶來祭牲把它宰殺是不夠的；血必須予以施用。基督復活昇天以後，“用自己的血，只一次進入聖所，成了永遠贖罪的事”（來9:12），並在那裡擔任“大祭司，……在聖所，就是真帳幕裡，作執事”（來8:1-3）。祂為我們服務。基督的這方面工作對於我們的救恩是不可少的，正如在第一個逾越節時羊羔的血，以及所有流血的祭牲所起的作用那樣。
贖罪大日的施血是每年崇事的高潮。祭牲的宰殺當然是很重要的，否則就無血可施。但最重要的時刻卻是大祭司帶著耶和華之羊的血進入至聖所（見來9:25）。同樣，基督“用自己的血，只一次進入聖所”（來9:12）。祂死在髑髏地是很重要的，否則祂就沒有“所獻的”了（來8:3）。但如果沒有天上聖所中不斷的施血，十字架上的犧牲就失去效果了。
大多數基督徒不理解也不欣賞基督擔任我們大祭司的工作。他們當然相信基督所流的血；但他們不明白，要想使血生效就必須施用血。現在正是將世人的注意力，特別是自稱為基督徒者的注意力轉到基督當前所作工作的時候。許多人在問基督為什麼耽擱這麼久時間。他們知道祂已經去了。但他們一點兒也不知道祂作中保的工作。他們沒有跟隨羔羊，也不知道祂現在在哪裡以及祂在做什麼。我們的職責和特權，我們作為一班百姓所受派的任務就是要重修古道（見賽58:12），告訴世人基督是我們的大祭司，在擔任中保的工作。祂的工作已快要完成了。完成以後，祂就要帶著能力和榮耀中降臨。

4.en: Sin is an offense against God. Man may sin against man, but his first and chief offense is against God. Hence, confession must always first be made to God. The prodigal son had sinned grievously against his father, yet when he returned his first words were, “I have sinned against heaven, and before thee” (Luke 15:18). He stated the matter rightly. Great as were his transgressions against men, his first offense was against God. This is the case in all sin. Through ignorance. That is, “unwittingly” (RSV), unintentionally, inadvertently, thoughtlessly, or carelessly. Against any of the commandments. This refers particularly to the Ten Commandments, but includes other commands of God as well. The entire sanctuary, including its equipment, its priesthood, and its ritual, was concerned with sin. The services revolved about man’s disobedience and need for salvation. Were it not for sin, there would be no need of an altar on which to place the victims; there would be no slaying of animals, no shedding of blood, no ministry of atonement. There would doubtless have been a place where man might meet with God, but the service would be of an altogether different nature. The evil of sin is not necessarily or only in the thing done. Nor is the same sin committed by different persons equally sinful. Light always brings responsibility, and the identical sin committed by an ignorant savage and by a highly civilized man must be considered and judged in each case from a different point of view. God takes all of this into consideration, and in the chapter before us makes provision for it. Accordingly, there is a certain gradation in the penalties imposed for sins committed by those holding different positions. The one who has light is held more responsible than the one who is in ignorance. In this chapter, four different classes of offenders are considered, and each is treated according to his standing. The sin of a prominent person affects more people than that of one less prominent; hence, it must be dealt with more severely. 4. Lay his hand. This was the same ceremony as in all animal sacrifices, except where fowls were used. The laying on of the hand denoted not merely the dedication of the animal to God; but as the offerer leaned heavily upon the head of the victim, he identified himself with it, and it became his substitute (see on ch. 1:4). The laying on of the hand was accompanied by a confession of the sin that had occasioned the bringing of the sacrifice (ch. 5:5). This principle applied to all sacrifices for sin. The act of laying on the hand was therefore significant, because the sinner in confessing his sin and leaning on the victim declared his faith in God, who provided a substitute to bear the penalty for his sin. The bringing of the sacrifice was not the penalty. The penalty was death, and this the animal paid.
4.zh:
他要牽公牛到會幕門口，在耶和華面前按手在牛的頭上，把牛宰於耶和華面前。

除了鳥類以外，所有的祭牲都要按手。按手在頭上不僅意味著把祭牲獻給上帝；而且當獻祭者重重地按手在祭牲的頭上時，他就與它融為一體，它成了他的替身（見利1:4註釋）。
隨著按手在祭牲頭上的，是承認導致獻祭的罪（利5:5）。這條原則適用於一切為罪所獻的祭物。所以按手在祭牲頭上是很重要的，因為罪人藉著承認自己的罪並靠在祭牲身上，宣佈他相信那提供替身承擔他罪罰的上帝。獻祭不是懲罰。懲罰是祭牲所受的死。

2.zh:
你曉諭以色列人說：若有人在耶和華所吩咐不可行的什麼事上誤犯了一件，

**犯。**第一次提到贖罪祭在有關亞倫和他兒子接受聖職的禮節中（出29:14），但當時沒有普及到百姓中去。“罪”和“贖罪祭”都譯自希伯來詞chatta'th，說明兩者之間的密切關係。既然有“罪”，就需要贖罪。獻贖罪祭暗示了罪已經犯了。一個人把“贖罪祭”帶到聖所，實際上就是將祭物所代表的罪帶到聖所來。祭物正是為贖罪而獻的。在講述建立聖所的和設立祭司職分時首先提到了贖罪祭。此前只有獻燔祭。聖經中界定和描述罪的各種詞彙提供了以下的概念：
一. 罪是偏離特定的標準，違背上帝的律法（約壹3:4）。如果我們把律法視為一條所要遵循的直線的話，那麼偏離這條線的都是罪。這種偏離既可能是偶然的，也可能是故意的，但無論如何這都是罪。
二. 罪就是虧欠，就是未能達到完美的目標。罪像一支沒有射中靶子的箭。弓箭手可能已經盡力了，但卻沒有足夠的力量來拉弓，使箭射中靶子。他虧缺了。“世人都犯了罪，虧缺了”（羅3:23）。
三. 罪就是悖逆。只有明知故犯才算悖逆。悖逆有不同的程度。上帝已為此做了準備。但所有的罪都是嚴重的。怙惡不悛的人罪終將犯下不可饒恕的罪。
四. 罪就是得罪上帝。人可能會得罪人，但他首先和主要是得罪上帝。所以人必須先向上帝懺悔。浪子嚴重得罪了他的父親，但他回家後的第一句話卻是：“我得罪了天，又得罪了你”（路15:18）。他說對了。雖然他嚴重得罪了人，但他首先是得罪了上帝。所有的罪都是如這樣。
**誤。**即“不故意的”，“小心輕率的”。
**什麼事上。**主要指十誡，也包括上帝的其他吩咐。
整個聖所，包括其中的器具，祭司的職分和禮儀都是與罪有關的。聖所的崇事都圍繞著人的悖逆和對救恩的需求上。若不是罪，就不必設立獻祭的壇了；就不需要宰殺祭牲、流祭牲的血和進行贖罪的崇事了。人無疑需要有一個與上帝相會的地方，但如果沒有罪，所進行的崇事將會是性質完全不同的。
罪惡不一定都是已經做出來的事情。相同的罪由不同的人犯下，其性質也是不一樣的。亮光總是伴隨著責任。一個無知的野蠻人和一個高度文明的人所犯相同的罪必須按不同的角度來評判。上帝把這一切都考慮在內，並在本章中作出了規定。對於不同地位之人，犯罪的處罰是有差別的。擁有亮光的人要比矇昧無知的人負有更多的責任。本章考慮到四等犯罪的人，並作出相應的處理。重要的人所犯的罪要比普通的人影響更多的人；所以要受更嚴厲的處罰。

13.zh:
以色列全會眾若行了耶和華所吩咐不可行的什麼事，誤犯了罪，是隱而未現，會眾看不出來的，

**全會眾。**個人可能經常犯罪並獻上必要的供物。但以色列民族作為一個整體，“誤犯了罪”的情況卻是很少的（見第2,6節註釋）。
**不可行的什麼事。**包括所有的罪，不論大小，但主要是指所謂的小罪。這裡所說的不是明顯的違法，而是一般“所吩咐不可行的什麼事”。這些事都會引發犯罪，所以必須把贖罪祭帶到聖所門口。

14.zh:
會眾一知道所犯的罪就要獻一隻公牛犢為贖罪祭，牽到會幕前。

這是以誤犯為前提的（見第2節註釋）。在這種情況下，“全會眾”要帶來與大祭司犯罪所獻相同的祭物。公牛犢的會眾所提供的，因為所有的人都算有罪。由各支派中選出的長老把公牛犢帶到獻祭的地方，按手在牛頭上，殺了它。這裡沒有提認罪。但按手就意味著認罪。若不認罪，所獻的祭就是無效的，因為罪還沒有從罪人轉到祭物身上。此外上帝所悅納的不是認罪的形式，而是認罪的內容。

17.zh:
把指頭蘸於血中，在耶和華面前對著幔子彈血七次，

血的施用與祭司犯罪時一樣（見第7節）。祭司用一個指頭施血，因此只用公牛犢一小部分的血。

19.zh:
把牛所有的脂油都取下，燒在壇上；

施血儀式結束以後，祭司將取下公牛犢所有的脂油，與大祭司犯罪時所採取的步驟相同（見第6-8節）。

20.zh:
收拾這牛，與那贖罪祭的牛一樣。祭司要為他們贖罪，他們必蒙赦免。

在受膏的祭司或大祭司的情況中，沒有提贖罪或赦罪。他認罪後，無疑和他人一樣會得到了赦免。但他是自己主持獻祭儀式的，看起來就像一個人能為自己贖罪似的，所以就省去了這樣的話。但這裡所涉及的是百姓，故祭司要“為他們贖罪，他們必蒙赦免”。把公牛犢帶到營外潔淨之處焚燒的儀式與受膏的祭司犯罪時一樣。

22.zh:
官長若行了耶和華─他神所吩咐不可行的什麼事，誤犯了罪，

“官長”指支派的首領或分支的首領，包括民事和宗教的領袖（創17:20；民2:3；民3:24,32；代下1:2）。官長可能不知道自己所犯的罪。一個官長對律法的認識比不上受膏的祭司或大祭司；所以他們要獻的祭物，價值低於大祭司所獻的。

24.zh:
按手在羊的頭上，宰於耶和華面前、宰燔祭牲的地方；這是贖罪祭。

這與獻其他祭物的方式和意義相同。罪人按手在祭牲頭上，與它融為一體，藉著認罪將自己的罪轉移給祭牲，讓它作為他的替身獻上。

25.zh:
祭司要用指頭蘸些贖罪祭牲的血，抹在燔祭壇的四角上，把血倒在燔祭壇的腳那裡。

施用山羊的血與施用公牛犢的不同。祭司不把血帶進聖所，而是把血接在一個器皿裡，帶到燔祭壇前，用指頭把血抹在壇的四角上。

26.zh:
所有的脂油，祭司都要燒在壇上，正如平安祭的脂油一樣。至於他的罪，祭司要為他贖了，他必蒙赦免。

不論是燔祭（利1:8），平安祭（利3:3），還是贖罪祭（利4:8），能取下的脂油都要焚燒在壇上。這樣，祭司就完成了他為犯罪的官長所做的工作，使他得到寬恕而離去。這裡沒有關於如何處置祭牲身體的指示。據利6:26，肉要歸給祭司，讓他在會幕院子的聖地裡吃掉。

5.en: The Lord’s passover. The Passover was not instituted until the deliverance of Israel from Egypt (Ex. 12:14, 27). It commemorated the saving power of God exercised in their behalf on that historic occasion, and was therefore for them “the Lord’s passover.” In striking contrast, “the sabbath of the Lord” became such when, at the close of creation week, God Himself rested upon that day and set it apart for the use and benefit of all mankind (Gen. 2:1–3; Ex. 20:8–11; Mark 2:27, 28). All men owe their very existence to the creative power of God and are therefore under obligation to Him to keep ever holy His appointed day of rest. As stated, the Passover was instituted in memory of Israel’s deliverance from Egyptian bondage. On the 10th day of the first month a lamb was selected for each household “according to the number of the souls,” or if the household was small, two or more households could unite for one sacrifice. The lamb was kept until the 14th day, when it was killed in the late afternoon, and its blood sprinkled on the doorposts (see on Ex. 12:1–10). The same night the flesh was eaten, not boiled as usual, but roasted. Only unleavened bread could be used, with bitter herbs (v. 8). In later years there were modifications in this ritual, but it remained essentially the same. The Passover sacrifice is distinguished by being called “my sacrifice” (Ex. 23:18; 34:25). The Passover commemorated Israel’s departure from Egypt. But it also looked forward to “Christ our Passover,” who was to be “sacrificed for us” (1 Cor. 5:7).In various respects the Passover fitly foreshadowed the crucifixion. At the crucifixion not a bone of Christ’s body was broken (John 19:36); not a bone of the Passover lamb might be broken (Ex. 12:46; Num. 9:12). The Passover lamb was slain the 14th day of Abib and eaten the same night (Ex. 12:6–10); Christ died at Passover time (John 19:14). The sprinkling of the blood meant a “passing over” in mercy, a deliverance from death (Ex. 12:13); so through Christ’s blood there has been a passing over of sins committed and confessed (Rom. 3:25). The Passover sacrifice was a lamb (Ex. 12:3); so Christ was “the Lamb of God” (John 1:29). The lamb was to be without blemish (Ex. 12:5); Christ was without blemish (1 Peter 1:19). Its flesh was to be eaten (Ex. 12:7); likewise we must partake of His flesh (John 6:51). The Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread are replete with gospel truth. In the slain lamb provision was made for saving the first-born. But the death of the lamb was not enough to assure salvation; the blood must be struck on the doorpost. The Passover is symbolic of Christ’s death. He is our Passover (1 Cor. 5:7). On the cross He made provision for everyone to be saved. But the cross in and of itself saves no one. It only made salvation available (see John 1:12). The death of the lamb provided the means of salvation; the application of the blood made efficacious the means provided. Both were necessary. Thus for the Christian the atonement on the cross, though essential and sufficient for all, does not save any individual until there has been an individual application of the blood. The sprinkling of the blood was fully as important as the death of the lamb. Yet even this was not enough; the flesh must be eaten, and it must be eaten under the specified conditions (Ex. 12:11). And this was not enough; all leaven must be purged away. Carelessness in the least particular would be fraught with tragic results (Ex. 12:13, 19, 23). It is one thing to be saved from death. It is another to have the means of sustaining life. This was provided positively by eating the lamb; negatively, by abstaining from leaven. Christ is “the living bread which came down from heaven,” of which a man must eat if he would “live for ever” (John 6:51). The lamb was to be roasted entire (Ex. 12:9). For each lamb there was to be a sufficient number of people so that all the flesh would be eaten (Ex. 12:4). Nothing was to be carried out of the house, and nothing left until morning. Whatever remained of those parts that could not be eaten was to be burned (Ex. 12:10, 46). Similarly, the Christian must assimilate completely the life of the One represented by the lamb. This means the entire identification of the believer with Christ. It means accepting fully the life and character of Jesus. The NT counterpart of the Passover is found in the Lord’s Supper, the communion service. After Christ had come, there could be no more virtue in slaying the Passover lamb, which prefigured His coming. But there would be virtue in commemorating the sacrifice of Calvary and its sustaining power. For this reason our Lord instituted the symbolic meal of communion, the purpose of which is to remind us of the provision made for our salvation upon the cross. Like its prototype, it points both backward and forward—we are to remember Calvary “till he come” (1 Cor. 11:26).
5.zh:
正月十四日，黃昏的時候，是耶和華的逾越節。

逾越節是以色列人從埃及得救以後制定的（出12:14,27）。它紀念上帝在那個歷史時刻為他們施展拯救的大能，所以對他們來說這是“耶和華的逾越節”。但“耶和華的安息日”是在創造周結束時設立的。上帝在那日安息，併為全人類的益處和使用而把它分別出來。（創2:1-3；出20:8-11；可2:27,28）。人類的存在都出於上帝創造的大能，所以他們有義務永遠尊祂所指定的安息日為聖。
如上所述，逾越節是為紀念以色列人脫離埃及的奴役而制定的。正月初十日，家家戶戶都要“按著人數”選定一隻羊羔。如果一家的人口太少，兩家或幾家人可以合用一隻祭牲。羊羔要到十四日黃昏才宰殺，把血被灑在門框上（見出12:1-10註釋）。當夜要把羊羔的肉吃掉，不是象平常那樣煮熟，而是用火烤熟。羊肉只能與無酵餅和苦菜同食（第8節）。後來這個禮節有所修改，但基本上是一樣的。
逾越節祭牲的獨特之處就是被稱為“我的祭牲”（出23:18；34:25）。逾越節既紀念以色列人出離埃及，也展望那將要“被殺獻祭”的“我們逾越節的羔羊基督”（林前5:7）。逾越節在各個方面都十分恰當地預表基督釘十字架。在十字架上，基督的身體連一根骨頭也沒有折斷（約19:36）；逾越節羊羔的骨頭也一根都不可折斷（出12:46；民9:12）。逾越節的羊羔是在亞筆月十四日被宰殺並在當夜吃掉的（出12:6-10）；基督也是在逾越節死的（約19:14）。灑血意味著憑恩典“逾越”，得救脫離死亡（出12:13）；同樣，憑著基督的血，也逾越了我們所已經承認的罪行（羅3:25）。逾越節的祭牲是一隻羊羔（出12:3）；基督也是“上帝的羔羊”（約1:29）。羊羔應當是無殘疾的（出12:5）；基督也是沒有瑕疵的（彼前1:19）。羊的肉要吃掉（出12:7）；我們也要分享祂的肉（約6:51）。
逾越節和除酵節充滿了福音的真理。羊羔的宰殺為頭生的得救做了預備。但羊羔的死還不足以保證得救；還需把血塗在門框上。
逾越節象徵基督的死。祂是我們逾越節的羔羊（林前5:7）。在十字架上，祂為每個人的得救做了準備。但十字架本身並不能自動地救人。它只是使救恩成為可能（見約1:12）。羔羊的死提供了拯救的手段；而血的應用使所提供的手段生效。兩者都是必不可少的。就基督徒而言，十字架上的贖罪雖然對於眾人來說是必要而充分的，但只有把血運用到個人身上發揮拯救的作用。灑血和羊羔的死一樣重要，但還不夠；還必須把肉吃掉，並且必須在特定的條件下吃掉（出12:11）。這還不夠；還要除淨所有的酵。任何一點的疏忽都將導致悲劇性的後果（出12:13,19,23）。
得救脫離死亡是一回事，擁有維持生命的手段則是另一回事。它的獲得，從正面說，是藉著吃羊羔的肉；從反面說，是藉著酵的除淨。基督是“從天上降下來生命的糧。”人若想“永遠活著”就必須吃這糧（約6:51）。羊羔要整隻用火烤（出12:9）。每一隻羊羔都應有足夠人數把它的肉吃完（出12:4）。不得把肉帶出房屋或留到早晨。吃剩下的肉都要燒掉（出12:10,46）。同樣，基督徒也必須完全吸收羊羔所象徵之主的生命。這意味著信徒與基督合而為一，完全接受耶穌的生命和品格。
在《新約》中與逾越節相對應的就是聖餐。基督來到以後， 宰殺預表祂來臨的逾越節羊羔就不再有用了。但紀念髑髏地的犧牲及其維持生命的能力仍是很有意義的。所以我們的主設立了象徵性的聖餐，其目的就是提醒我們十字架為我們所預備的救法。和它所象徵的對像一樣，它具有瞻前顧後的意義──我們應當紀念髑髏地“直等到他來”（林前11:26）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》42；《善惡之爭》399；《先祖與先知》537.539。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》42；《善惡之爭》399；《先祖與先知》537.539。

3.en: Sabbath of rest. Literally “a sabbath of sabbath observance.” Our translation fails to convey the full force of the original Hebrew, which is variously translated a “sabbath of deep rest,” “a sabbath of complete rest,” “a perfect sabbath,” “a sabbath of solemn rest” (RSV). The Sabbath is different from all the other feasts and holy convocations (see vs. 37, 38) in that it originated at creation (Gen. 2:1–3), whereas the annual feasts and “sabbaths” had their origin with the Jewish nation. The seventh-day Sabbath “was made for man” (Mark 2:27), and hence is of obligation for all men forever; the annual feasts were made for the Jews and ceased to be of obligation when type met Antitype at the death of Christ (Col. 2:16, 17). The seventh-day Sabbath is incorporated in the law of God, the Ten Commandments, His constitution for this world. Because it was made before sin entered, it will remain after sin is no more (Isa. 66:22, 23). On the other hand, the annual Jewish feasts were of only temporal, local, ceremonial application, fitted to conditions in Palestine, and could not be made of worldwide application. Thus the Feast of First Fruits (of winter crops), celebrated in late spring, in May, could not be observed in the southern hemisphere till six months later. Similarly, it would not be possible for people in all lands to observe the Feast of Tabernacles in the autumn. The Jews have found that it is not even possible for them to observe the Day of Atonement as ordered by God, except in connection with the Temple. The Passover could appropriately be observed in anticipation of a coming Redeemer, but not after His coming. All these feasts served their purpose, adapted as they were to the needs of the Jews while they lived in Palestine, prior to the coming of Messiah. They have ceased, but the seventh-day Sabbath remains. To make sure that the Sabbath should not be considered a Jewish institution, and hence cease with the Jewish nation, Christ emphatically declared, “The sabbath was made for man” (Mark 2:27). He added, “Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath” (v. 28). It belongs to Him; He is “Lord” of it. Let none tamper with it, for they have no right to do so. It is “my holy day,” says God (Isa. 58:13). The sabbath of the Lord. This is the equivalent of, “it is the Lord’s sabbath,” and indicates proprietorship. If God should have spoken of the first day of the week as “my holy day,” or “the sabbath of the Lord,” none today would be uncertain as to what He meant. Instead, He uses these very expressions in regard to the seventh day. It is His day.
3.zh:
六日要做工，第七日是聖安息日，當有聖會；你們什麼工都不可做。這是在你們一切的住處向耶和華守的安息日。

**聖安息日。**意為“深深安息的安息日”，“完全安息的安息日”，“完全的安息日”，“嚴肅安息的安息日”。
安息日與其他所有的節期和聖會都不同（見第37,38節），因為它起源於創造（創2:1-3），而年度的節期和假日則起源於猶太民族。第七日的安息日“是為人設立的”（可2:27），所以全人類永遠需要遵守。年度的節期是為猶太人設立的，當基督受死，預表遇到實體時，就不再需要遵守了（西2:16,17）。第七日的安息日列入賜給這個世界的憲法——十誡之中。它是罪惡進入世界以前設立的，所以要存留到罪惡消滅以後（賽66:22,23）。而年度的猶太節期只是臨時性，地區性的，儀文性的，只適合巴勒斯坦的環境，不適用於全球的範圍。
所以春末五月份慶祝的（冬季莊稼）初熟節在南半球要推遲六個月。同樣，世界各地的人也不可能都在秋季守住棚節。猶太人發現連贖罪日都難以按上帝的吩咐遵守，除非是在聖殿。遵守逾越節是為了期待將來的救贖主，故不適於祂來以後。這些節期都有其目的，符合彌賽亞來臨之前猶太人在巴勒斯坦時的需求。它們已經失效了，但第七日的安息日依然存在。
為了確保安息日不被視為猶太人的制度，隨著猶太的亡國而廢除，基督強調說：“安息日是為人設立的”（可2:27）。祂又補充說：“因此人子也是安息日的主”（第28節）。安息日是屬於祂的；祂是它的“主”。任何人都不得篡改它，因為他們無權這樣做。上帝說，這是“我的聖日”（賽58:13）。
**向耶和華守的安息日。**就是“耶和華的安息日”，表明所有權。如果上帝說七日的第一日是“我的聖日”或“向耶和華守的安息日”，今日就不會有人對祂的話質疑了。但祂指的是第七日。這是祂的日子。

24.en: Blowing the trumpets. On the first day of the seventh month was a sabbath; “an holy convocation” was to be held. On that day the trumpets were blown, for the Day of Atonement was near at hand, and the first nine days of the month were to be days of preparation for it. The first day of the seventh month of the religious calendar was new year’s day, the first day of the civil calendar year.
24.zh:
你曉諭以色列人說：七月初一，你們要守為聖安息日，要吹角作記念，當有聖會。

七月初一日要守為安息日，舉行“聖會”，吹響號角，因為贖罪日近了。這個月的頭九天要為贖罪日作準備。宗教歷的七月初一日是民事歷的元旦。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖和君王》661。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖和君王》661。

27.en: A day of atonement. This day was the only commanded fast (see Acts 27:9). It was a high day in Israel, and is called a “sabbath of rest” (Lev. 23:32). It was the only day, aside from the weekly Sabbath, on which all work was forbidden.
27.zh:
七月初十是贖罪日；你們要守為聖會，並要刻苦己心，也要將火祭獻給耶和華。

這是唯一指定禁食的日子（見徒27:9）。在以色列人中，這是個大日，被稱為“聖安息日”（利23:32）。除了每週的安息日以外，這是唯一禁止作任何工的日子。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》448，757；《善惡之爭》418；《證言》卷五520。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》448，757；《善惡之爭》418；《證言》卷五520。

7.en: No servile work. The first and last days of the feast were days of holy convocation on which no “laborious work” (RSV) might be done. Each day two bullocks were offered, one ram, and seven lambs for a burnt offering, with their accompanying cereal offerings, and one goat for a sin offering (Num. 28:19–24).
7.zh:
第一日當有聖會，什麼勞碌的工都不可做；

該節期的第一天和最後一天當有聖會，什麼勞碌的工都不可做。每天要獻兩隻公牛犢，一隻公綿羊和七隻公羊羔為燔祭，還有同獻的素祭，以及一隻山羊為贖罪祭（民28:19-24）。

2.en: Feasts of the Lord. The annual “set feasts” (Num. 29:39) are six in number: (1) the Passover (Num. 28:16); (2) the Feast of Unleavened Bread (Num. 28:17); (3) the “feast of harvest,” the “feast of weeks” (first fruits), or Pentecost (Ex. 23:16; 34:22; Num. 28:26; Acts 2:1); (4) the Feast of Trumpets (Num. 29:1); (5) the Day of Atonement (Num. 29:7); (6) the “feast of ingathering,” the “feast of tabernacles” (Ex. 23:16; Lev. 23:34; Num. 29:12). With these six feasts are seven days of “holy convocation”; the first and last days of the Feast of Unleavened Bread (Num. 28:18, 25); the day of first fruits (Num. 28:26); the Feast of Trumpets (Num. 29:1); the Day of Atonement (Num. 29:7); the first and last days of the Feast of Tabernacles (Lev. 23:35, 36). The word translated “feast” in this chapter is from one or the other of two Hebrew words: (1) Mo‘ed, an appointed meeting (used, for example, in Lev. 23:2, 4, 37; Num. 29:39). (2) Chag, a festival (used, for example, in Lev. 23:6, 34, 39, 41; Num. 28:17; 29:12). The two words are sometimes used interchangeably, though mo‘ed stresses the time of the feast, “set feasts” (Num. 29:39); chag, the character of the feast. Chag is derived from a verb that has, as one of its possible meanings, “to make a pilgrimage,” “to take a journey to an object of reverence.” The related Arabic word haj describes the sacred Moslem pilgrimage to Mecca. In the listing of the annual “set feasts,” chag, significantly, is used only of three, the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of First Fruits, and the Feast of Tabernacles. “Three times shalt thou keep a feast [chag] unto me in the year” (Ex. 23:14). To celebrate these three feasts all males were to “appear before the Lord in the place which he shall choose” (Deut. 16:16). They were to “make a pilgrimage.” There is therefore no contradiction between the statement in Exodus, that the Israelites were to “keep a feast” “three times” “in the year” (Ex. 23:14), and the listing, in Leviticus, of six annual feasts (see also Num. 28, 29). Each of these six feasts is described as a mo‘ed, but three of them are also designated chag. In other words, there were six mo‘ed but only three chag. The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia describes these three as “pilgrimage festivals.” Though the Passover may be properly listed as a separate “appointed meeting,” a mo‘ed, it may also be considered a part of the Feast of Unleavened Bread. The Passover lamb was slain on the 14th of the first month and eaten that night, in the beginning of the 15th, the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread. The Passoverand the Feast of Unleavened Bread were really two parts of one whole, and in some instances were thus considered (see Exe. 45:21). In view of this we might speak of five, rather than six, annual feasts.
2.zh:
你曉諭以色列人說：耶和華的節期，你們要宣告為聖會的節期。

一年一度的“節期”（民29:39）共有六個：一，逾越節（民28:16）；二，除酵節（民28:17）；三，“收割節”，即“七七節”（初熟節）或五旬節（出23:16；34:22；民28:26；徒2:1）；四，吹角節（民29:1）；五，贖罪日（民29:7）；六，“收藏節”，即“住棚節”（出23:16；利23:34；民29:12）。
在這六個節期中有七天“聖會”；除酵節的第一天和最後一天（民28:18,25）；七七節（民28:26）；吹角節（民29:1）；贖罪日（民29:7）；住棚節的第一天和最後一天（利23:35,36）。
“節期”的原文有兩個：一，Mo'ed，意為“指定的聚會”（用於利23:2,4,37；民29:39等）。二，Chag，節日（用於利23:6,34,39,41；民28:17；29:12等）。這兩個詞有時可以互換使用。但mo'ed強調的是節日的時間（民29:39）；chag強調的是節日的性質。Chag源於一個動詞，其含義之一是“朝聖”。相應的阿拉伯詞haj指穆斯林到麥迦朝聖。在年度的“節期”中，chag只用於除酵節，初熟節和住棚節。“一年三次，你要向我守節[chag]”（出23:14）。為了慶祝這三個節期，所有的男丁都要“在耶和華你上帝所選擇的地方朝見他”（申16:16）。他們要“朝聖”。
因此《出埃及記》所說的以色列人要一年守節三次（出23:14）與《利未記》中一年六個節期並沒有矛盾（另見民28,29）。這六個節期都被稱為mo'ed，但其中的三個也可稱為chag。換一句話說，一年共有六個mo'ed，但只有三個chag。《國際標準聖經百科全書》稱這三個節期為“朝聖的節日”。
逾越節雖然可以算為一個單獨的mo'ed （“指定的聚會”），但也可視為除酵節的一部分。因為逾越節的羊羔是在正月十四日宰殺，並在當天晚上，也就是除酵節的第一天（正月十五日）的開始吃掉的。逾越節和除酵節實際上是一個整體的兩個部分。有時也是這樣看的（見結45:21）。所以我們也可以說年度的節期是五個而不是六個。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》41。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》41。

1.zh:
耶和華對摩西說：

**懷愛倫註釋（1–44節）**。《教育論》41-43；《先祖與先知》537-542。

6.zh:
這月十五日是向耶和華守的無酵節；你們要吃無酵餅七日。

與逾越節緊密相關但又有區別的是隨之而來的無酵節。實際上這兩個節期被視為一個，它們的名稱也經常互換，但它們的目的卻有些不同。逾越節象徵拯救（出12:13）；無酵餅則紀念以色列人出埃及時的匆忙（出12:33,39；申16:3）。上帝詳細說明了紀念無酵節的方法（出12:15）。關於這個節日，保羅後來說：“我們守這節不可用舊酵，也不可用惡毒、邪惡的酵，只用誠實真正的無酵餅”（林前5:8）。
酵要完全除掉。它象徵著惡毒和邪惡（林前5:8），以及在法利賽人，撒都該人和希律黨人的教訓中所宣揚的假道理（太16:6,12；可8:15）。法利賽人的酵就是貪婪和不義（太23:14），攔在天國門口不讓人進來（第13節），假熱心（第15節），對屬靈價值的錯誤認識（第16-22節），缺乏公義、憐憫和信實（第23節），無謂的謹慎（第24節），假冒為善（第25-28節），狹隘（第29-33節）和殘酷（第34-36節）。撒都該人的酵是懷疑主義（太22:23）和不瞭解聖經以及上帝的大能（第29節）。希律黨人的酵就是阿諛，世俗化和偽善（第16-21節），並且陰謀陷害上帝的代表（可3:6）。

10.zh:
你曉諭以色列人說：你們到了我賜給你們的地，收割莊稼的時候，要將初熟的莊稼一捆帶給祭司。

奉獻初熟之物是無酵節慶典活動的一部分。時間是在“安息日的次日”，即亞筆月十六日（利23:11）。這一天既沒有“聖會”也不是“安息日”，但有一件重要的工作要在完成。在亞筆月十四日要標出一塊麥田準備收割在十六日奉獻。三個被選中的人在證人面前割下大麥。這幾捆大麥在收割以前就已經捆了起來。收割以後，這些麥子捆成一大捆，獻在耶和華面前作為“初熟的莊稼一捆”。還要把一隻完美的公綿羊羔，調油的素祭和奠祭獻給上帝（第12,13節）。這一切都完成以後，以色列人才可以享用田間的出產。這個禮節指出“初熟的果子是基督，以後在祂來的時候，是那些屬基督的”（林前15:23）。

14.zh:
無論是餅，是烘的子粒，是新穗子，你們都不可吃，直等到把你們獻給神的供物帶來的那一天才可以吃。這在你們一切的住處作為世世代代永遠的定例。

逾越節的儀式強調了基督教偉大的核心真理。逾越節象徵基督的死。正如逾越節的羊羔死了，基督也死了。羊羔的血從滅命天使的手下拯救了古時的以色列人。如今基督的血現在也使一切憑著信心到祂面前來的人與上帝和好。
逾越節還象徵復活，正如搖祭的禾捆所預表的。羊羔死於亞筆月十四日。到十六日，就是“安息日的次日”，收割好的初熟之物要獻在耶和華面前。基督也在星期五下午死去，在安息日安息在墳墓裡（路23:53-56）。到安息日的次日（路24:1），“初熟的果子”基督（林前15:20）從墳墓中復活了，並將自己獻在天父面前（約20:17）。
“安息日的次日”（利23:11）無論在預表還是在實體中，都沒有“聖會”，也不是“安息日”，但在那日有一項重要的工作要完成。基督在七日的第一日復活，升到天父那裡去，聽上帝說悅納祂犧牲的話。
逾越節還促進團契生活。吃逾越節的羊羔使家人和鄰舍都聚在一起。這是象徵拯救，呼籲獻身的聚餐。一切罪惡都必須放棄。任何酵都不得留在家中。每一個角落都必須檢查以免有酵。除了完全“歸耶和華為聖”的東西以外，任何其他東西都不會蒙悅納（見詩29:2；96:9）。逾越節是一個非常嚴肅的場合。
逾越節對於古代以色列人具有上述甚至更多的意義。聖餐今天對於我們也是這樣。我們很容易忘記或不領會上帝為那些正確參加聖殿儀式的人所存留的奇妙福氣。我們應當認真研究賜給以色列人的逾越節，以便更加理解那逾越節的真羔羊。我們的聖餐就是紀念祂的主。

15.zh:
你們要從安息日的次日，獻禾捆為搖祭的那日算起，要滿了七個安息日。

**七個安息日。**就是七週（見第16節）。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–17節）**。《先祖與先知》540。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–17節）**。《先祖與先知》540。

16.zh:
到第七個安息日的次日，共計五十天，又要將新素祭獻給耶和華。

“七七節”或“初熟節”（出34:22）在亞筆月十六日獻禾捆為搖祭以後的第五十天，也就是在三月初六日，即公曆的五月底或六月初。它在新約時代稱為“五旬節”，源於希臘詞語“五十”。
正如在收割開始，享用新收成的糧食以前要獻搖祭，五旬節標誌著收割季節的結束，儘管在山區有些莊稼可能還有待收割。以色列人藉此歡樂地承認自己仰賴上帝賜予一切美好的禮物。這時所獻的不是一捆莊稼，而是兩張加酵的烤細麵餅作為搖祭。還有七隻公羊羔，一隻公牛犢和兩隻公綿羊（利23:17,18）。另外還要一隻山羊為贖罪祭；兩隻公綿羊羔為平安祭（第19節）。
逾越節的慶典中不可吃酵，百姓家中也不可有酵。但五旬節所獻的兩張餅卻要“加酵、烤成”（第17節）。作為搖祭的禾捆乃是“初熟的莊稼”基督（見第14節註釋）。祂是無罪的。
五旬節象徵聖靈的沛降。正如搖祭的餅是在作為搖祭的禾捆獻上五十天以後奉獻的，基督復活和五旬節的聖靈沛降也相隔五十天（徒2:1-4）。其中四十天基督在地上教訓和幫助祂的門徒（徒1:3）。然後祂昇天了。十一位門徒在接下的十天裡繼續祈禱懇求，直到“五旬節到了”。隨之而來的是聖靈的充滿（徒1:8；2:4）。門徒在五旬節的工作加在基督的工作之上，結果使天國大得榮耀。
這十天對於地上的教會是十分重要的，對於天上也是很重要的。當基督“升上高天的時候，擄掠了仇敵，將各樣的恩賜賞給人”（弗4:8）。那些在基督受死時起來的聖徒，“在耶穌復活以後，他們從墳墓裡出來”，與祂一同昇天，然後被獻在聖父面前作為復活的初熟果子（太27:52,53）。

22.zh:
在你們的地收割莊稼，不可割盡田角，也不可拾取所遺落的；要留給窮人和寄居的。我是耶和華─你們的神。

本節重複利19:9,10的吩咐。在豐收的時節，應該對窮人和外人格外的關照。

29.zh:
當這日，凡不刻苦己心的，必從民中剪除。

贖罪日也是一個審判的日子。凡不“刻苦己心”的，都要被“剪除”（見創17:14；出12:15註釋）。如果有人在那日做工，上帝就要消滅他。關於贖罪日的遵守，詳見第16章註釋。

32.zh:
你們要守這日為聖安息日，並要刻苦己心。從這月初九日晚上到次日晚上，要守為安息日。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一116；《證言》卷六355。

34.zh:
你曉諭以色列人說：這七月十五日是住棚節，要在耶和華面前守這節七日。

這是宗教年曆一年中最後的節期，通常是在公曆十月份，秋收結束，莊稼已經收藏好的時候。這是一個大家歡樂的時刻。贖罪日已經結束；一切誤會都已消除；罪惡都已承認並被拋棄。以色列人非常高興。這種高興在住棚節表達出來。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》447，《教育論》42。
**懷愛倫註釋（34–36節）**。《先知和君王》665；《先祖與先知》540。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》447，《教育論》42。
**懷愛倫註釋（34–36節）**。《先知和君王》665；《先祖與先知》540。

40.zh:
第一日要拿美好樹上的果子和棕樹上的枝子，與茂密樹的枝條並河旁的柳枝，在耶和華─你們的神面前歡樂七日。

用這些枝子來搭建以色列人住棚節所住的棚子。百姓在贖罪日要刻苦己心，但在住棚節則要“歡樂”。這是一年中最快樂的時刻。朋友和鄰舍要和諧相愛地住在一起，親密交往。在這方面，它預表上帝子民的大會聚，“從東從西，將有許多人來，在天國裡與亞伯拉罕、以撒、雅各，一同坐席”（太8:11）。
住棚節紀念以色列人四十年在曠野飄流住帳棚的日子（見申16:12-15）。
我們應當記住上帝過去曾如何引導我們。不要忘記祂的眷顧，因為我們有時會抱怨祂今天引領我們的方式。我們難道不應該思考上帝賜給我們的眾多福氣，以及祂引導我們的奇妙方式嗎？這樣，我們就會更加感恩。感恩是宗教的一個重要部分。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》291。
**懷愛倫註釋（40–43節）**。《先祖與先知》540。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》291。
**懷愛倫註釋（40–43節）**。《先祖與先知》540。

9.en: Do not drink. This prohibition suggests the cause of the transgression. It seems hardly reasonable to believe that God would issue such an edict at this time and under these circumstances except to clarify the true cause of the tragedy. Lest ye die. Death was the most severe penalty that could be meted out, and stressed God’s attitude toward the use of strong drink. The sin of the young men was not a light matter that could be erased by the offering of a sacrifice. It was deliberate, and reflected scorn for sacred things. It was a major sin and deserved drastic punishment.
9.zh:
你和你兒子進會幕的時候，清酒、濃酒都不可喝，免得你們死亡；這要作你們世世代代永遠的定例。

**不可喝。**這條禁令暗示這次犯罪的起因。上帝在當時的狀況下發布這樣一條命令，似乎令人難以置信，除非是為了說明悲劇的真正原因。
**免得你們死亡。**死亡是最嚴厲的懲罰。這裡強調上帝對飲酒的態度。這兩個年輕人所犯的罪不是獻祭所能消除的小事，而是故意的犯罪，是對聖物的藐視。這是大罪，應當受到嚴厲的制裁。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–11節）**。《先祖與先知》362；《論節制》44，268，28。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–11節）**。《先祖與先知》362；《論節制》44，268，28。

2.en: Fire from the Lord. The effect upon the people gathered for the hour of prayer must have been profound. A few months previously Israel had witnessed the great display of God’s power at the giving of the law; then they apostatized and worshiped the golden calf. God was ready to disown them, but at Moses’ pleading they were again restored. Now they had built the tabernacle, which had been accepted, and God had shown His pleasure in the spirit of devotion it represented by sending fire to consume the offering. And now at the time of the evening sacrifice, when the people were gathered expectantly, the stroke came. Two of Aaron’s sons were dead. Rejoicing was turned into grief and perplexity. Had God forsaken them? What did this tragedy mean?
2.zh:
就有火從耶和華面前出來，把他們燒滅，他們就死在耶和華面前。

這一定給聚集祈禱的百姓帶來極大的震撼。幾個月前，以色列人在頒佈律法時曾目睹上帝大能的顯示；後來他們背道去敬拜金牛犢。上帝準備拋棄他們。但在摩西的懇求下他們得到了寬恕。現在，他們建立了帳幕。帳幕也已蒙悅納。上帝降下火來燒盡供物，表示祂喜悅他們的奉獻精神。現在，正當百姓懷著期待的心情聚集舉行晚祭的時候，這一打擊突然臨到。亞倫的兩個兒子死了。喜樂變為悲哀和困惑。上帝難道棄絕了他們？這場悲劇意味著什麼呢？
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育原理》428；《傳道良助》20；《先祖與先知》369。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–3節）**。《文字佈道士》91。

10.en: Put difference. Wine and strong drink can so benumb the faculties that a man fails to make a clear distinction between right and wrong, between holy and unholy, between clean and unclean. This had led the two sons to take common fire as they entered the sanctuary; in their condition they could see no difference. And as far as men could see, there was no difference. Fire was fire, was it not? But God looked on their hearts and saw something that men could not see. There was a difference. Similarly, the first day of the week is as good as the seventh day, to human reasoning. There is no difference—except in God’s command. And that makes a vital difference, a difference between life and death. Any form of intemperance blurs the difference between the holy and unholy, and between the clean and unclean, between the right and wrong. The use of spiritous liquors affects all the faculties and disturbs the orderly processes of the mind. He who drives and drinks is a menace to himself and to others, and a potential murderer. His mind is confused, his reflexes are slow, his sight is unreliable, and his sense of responsibility has all but vanished. The danger is not confined to those who are actually “drunk.” Even a small amount of liquor may cause disaster. The moderate drinker is a social liability, and may do untold harm. The very fact, of which he boasts, that he can “hold” his liquor and control himself, may lead others to think they can do the same. The drunkard wallowing in his filth may disgust the onlooker and thus serve as a warning. The moderate drinker tempts others to follow him by the very fact that he stays “respectable.” Of the two, the moderate drinker, in the end, does the more harm. Not only are the physical faculties affected by drink, but the moral as well; and this may be the worse of two evils. Assault, murder, rape, disloyalty, take on another aspect to the man who drinks. Under the influence of wine men will do what they would never consider doing were they sober. Only the judgment will reveal the sin of intoxication in its true dimensions. God’s warning to Aaron and his sons is fully applicable today. Men cannot drink and yet have a clear perception of the difference between the holy and the unholy, between the clean and the unclean (Isa. 28:7). This instruction is particularly addressed to leaders. Teaching is more than oral instruction; it includes example as well as precept. But what if the teacher’s own sense of right and wrong is blurred, and his conduct belies his words? Of all men, those who teach others, whether in state or church, must have a constantly alert mind, ready to cope with whatever problems may come before them. As we consider some of the decisions arrived at in councils of state, and know of the liquor consumed on such occasions, we are reminded that God’s counsel not to drink wine or strong drink is present truth.
10.zh:
使你們可以將聖的、俗的，潔淨的、不潔淨的，分別出來；

清酒和濃酒會麻木人的感官，使人不能辯別是非、聖俗、潔淨與不潔淨的。因此這兩個兒子拿著凡火進入聖所。他們當時看不出區別。這種區別人是看不出來的。火就是火，難道不是嗎？但上帝所看到的是他們的內心，是人所看不見的東西。那是有區別的。同樣，在人看來，每週的第一日和第七日是一樣的，沒有什麼區別，除了上帝誡命的吩咐之外。但這是重要的區別，是生死之別。
任何形式的不節制都會模糊聖俗、是非、潔淨與不潔淨之間的區別。飲酒會影響所有的感官並擾亂大腦的正常運轉。酒後駕車會給自己和他人帶來威脅。這是一種潛在的殺手。因為他思維混亂，反應遲鈍，視力模糊，責任感消失了。
危險不限於那些真正“喝醉”的人。即使少量喝酒也可能造成災難。適度飲酒已成為一種時尚，帶來了莫可言喻的危害。他所矜誇能控制酒量並把握自己的說法，使別人也以為自己能做到這一點。醉漢倒在自己的汙穢中令路人厭惡，從而起到警示的作用。但飲酒適度的人以其仍能“保持體面”來誘惑別人效法。相比之下，適度飲酒的人危害更大。
飲酒不僅影響身體的機能，也影響人的道德。這是更嚴重的惡果。飲酒會誘發人身的傷害、謀殺、強姦和不忠的行為。在酒精的影響下，人會做出清醒時絕不會去做的事情。只有上帝的懲罰顯示出醉酒之罪的真實性質。上帝對亞倫和他兒子的警告完全適用於今天。喝酒的人不可能清楚地辨別聖與俗、潔淨與不潔淨（賽28:7）。
這條吩咐是特別針對領袖們的。他們不但要言傳，也要身教。如果教師自己是非不分，言行不一，那會怎麼樣呢？在所有的人中，教導別人的人，不論是在國家還是在教會中，都必須時刻保持清醒的頭腦，隨時應付出現在面前的問題。鑑於議會中所作出的一些決議，以及這些場合中所消耗的酒量，我們就會知道，上帝禁止人喝清酒或濃酒是很現實的真理。

1.en: Nadab and Abihu. These were two of the sons of Aaron, and hence nephews of Moses. Next to Moses and Aaron they occupied the highest positions in Israel and had many advantages and privileges. They had heard the voice of God; they had been with Moses and Aaron in the mount of God; they had seen the God of Israel, and “did eat and drink” (Ex. 24:9–11). They had been greatly favored; but had not profited by their opportunities. Shortly before the events noted in this chapter they had spent a week in study and meditation, preparing for the day when they should begin their sanctuary service. They had assisted their father as he offered sacrifices, and had brought the blood of the victims to him (Lev. 9:9). They had witnessed the solemn service of dedication, and had themselves been sprinkled with sacrificial blood. They had been thoroughly indoctrinated, and were fully acquainted with the sacredness of God’s work. All of this only made their sin the greater. They were without excuse. When the time came for them to officiate, they did that which the Lord their God “commanded them not.” Strange fire. Ordinary fire. It was not taken from the altar of burnt offering, whose fire God Himself had kindled and which was therefore sacred (ch. 16:12, 13). In the court of the congregation there were hearths where the priests prepared their food, and it may be that Nadab and Abihu took their common fire from thence.
1.zh:
亞倫的兒子拿答、亞比戶各拿自己的香爐，盛上火，加上香，在耶和華面前獻上凡火，是耶和華沒有吩咐他們的，

**拿答和亞比戶。**是亞倫的兒子，也是摩西的侄子。他們在以色列人中的地位僅次於摩西和亞倫，享有許多優惠和特權。他們曾聽過上帝的聲音，與摩西和亞倫一同在上帝的山上，見過以色列的上帝，並且“又吃又喝”（出24:9-11）。他們得到過很大的好處，卻沒有受益於他們的機會。
在本章所記載的事件以前不久，他們曾用一週的時間進行研究和默想，為他們開始在聖所中服務的日子做準備。他們曾協助他們的父親獻祭，並把祭牲的血奉給他（利9:9）。他們見證了奉獻禮的莊嚴崇事，自己也曾被祭牲的血所灑。他們得到過充分的指示，完全瞭解上帝工作的神聖性。這一切都使他們的罪更顯嚴重。他們是不可原諒的。到了他們主持儀式的時候，他們做了耶和華他們的上帝“沒有吩咐他們的”事。
**凡火。**就是普通的火。不是從燔祭壇上取下來的。燔祭壇的火是上帝親自所點燃的，因此而成為聖火（利16:12,13）。在會幕的院子裡有祭司預備食物用的灶具。拿答和亞比戶可能就是從這裡取的凡火。

3.zh:
於是摩西對亞倫說：這就是耶和華所說：我在親近我的人中要顯為聖；在眾民面前，我要得榮耀。亞倫就默默不言。

摩西所指的可能是出19:22的話：“叫……祭司自潔，恐怕我忽然出來擊殺他們。”亞倫的兒子顯然沒有自潔。獻身擔任祭司並沒有使他們的內心發生變化；他們依然是“凡”的。
亞倫懦弱縱容的性情是這次不幸的根源。想到幾個月以前自己的軟弱，他一定深感不安。的確，上帝已赦免了他，悅納了他的贖罪祭；但他沒有藉著悔改消除他軟弱的後果。他沒有采取相應的步驟。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《傳道良助》20；《先祖與先知》361。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《傳道良助》20；《先祖與先知》361。

6.zh:
摩西對亞倫和他兒子以利亞撒、以他瑪說：不可蓬頭散髮，也不可撕裂衣裳，免得你們死亡，又免得耶和華向會眾發怒；只要你們的弟兄以色列全家為耶和華所發的火哀哭。

按當時的習俗，人在極其悲傷的時候要撕裂衣裳，就是撕裂衣裳的前胸，似乎象徵心裡悲傷。亞倫和他其餘的兒子不可以這樣做，因為這看起來像是對上帝懲罰的不滿。他們也不可蓬頭散發。這也是東方人表示悲傷的慣常做法。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》708。
**懷愛倫註釋（6–7節）**。《先祖與先知》361。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》708。
**懷愛倫註釋（6–7節）**。《先祖與先知》361。

7.zh:
你們也不可出會幕的門，恐怕你們死亡，因為耶和華的膏油在你們的身上。他們就照摩西的話行了。

亞倫十分難過，默默地來往主持晚祭和獻香，但沒有在言語或舉止上表示出悲傷。當百姓看到他照常平靜地工作時，就知道這兩個兒子不的不幸並沒有削弱亞倫對上帝的信心。他們可能不明白，正是亞倫的鎮靜消除了他們的恐懼，並恢復了他們的信心。

11.zh:
又使你們可以將耶和華藉摩西曉諭以色列人的一切律例教訓他們。

**使你們可以……教訓。**祭司乃是教師。他們的工作就是要把上帝的律例和典章教導百姓。但如果他們自己都無法分辨是非的話，又怎能從事這項工作呢？糊塗的頭腦是不可能教訓或引領他人行走所當走的路上的。
**借摩西曉諭。**直今仍有人貶低摩西。他們應該明白，是上帝藉著他說話，用這些話語認證了他的生活和工作。基督說：“你們如果信摩西，也必信我；……你們若不信他的書，怎能信我的話呢？”（約5:46,47）。的確有些規定是單為以色列人的，適用於當地的情況。但這是很容易辨別的。上帝“借摩西”所傳達的永恆原則始終具有同樣的效力和價值。每一位基督徒務要思考基督的話：“你們若不信他的書，怎能信我的話呢？”這句話不可視之等閒，因為這是基督說的。

13.zh:
你們要在聖處吃；因為在獻給耶和華的火祭中，這是你的分和你兒子的分；所吩咐我的本是這樣。

在兩個兒子的死亡所帶來的忙亂中，亞倫忘記了吃素祭中屬於他的那一份。悲劇的發生不應影響所規定的儀式。工作必須照常進行。

14.zh:
所搖的胸，所舉的腿，你們要在潔淨地方吃。你和你的兒女都要同吃；因為這些是從以色列人平安祭中給你，當你的分和你兒子的分。

這個特定的素祭顯然包括平安祭，因為亞倫的女兒也有份（利9:17-21）。素祭是至聖的，只有祭司才可以吃。至於平安祭，全家人和其他“潔淨”的人都可以分享。

15.zh:
所舉的腿，所搖的胸，他們要與火祭的脂油一同帶來當搖祭，在耶和華面前搖一搖；這要歸你和你兒子，當作永得的分，都是照耶和華所吩咐的。

任何事情都不得阻止上帝的工作，任何環境不得妨礙聖所的儀式，隨著年歲的流逝，這個觀念要深深紮根在祭司的腦海中。公元70年聖殿最終被羅馬人攻佔和毀滅的時候，這一點經受了最嚴峻的考驗。那正是獻晚祭的時候。耶路撒冷已被攻佔，但聖殿依然完好。當羅馬人攀過圍牆進入聖殿的區域時，祭司們仍在莊嚴而鎮靜地舉行了獻祭的儀式。建築物被焚燒，到處都是火焰。但祭司們卻邁著緩慢而整齊的步伐繼續他們的工作，對周圍的一切連看也不看。任何事情都不能妨礙上帝的工作。
王室也要學習同樣的功課。在王家馬車附近可能有一枚炸彈爆炸，但國王卻不可理睬。他必須保持鎮定，不受任何干擾，繼續前進，不要回頭觀看。
耶穌對一些把個人的事情擺在首位的門徒所作的回答似乎有些生硬和無情（見路9:59-62）。沒有什麼義務比照顧父母更重要的了。但就連這些義務──它們可以稱之為神聖的義務──也不能阻擋履行上帝聖工的道路。工作必須繼續進行。

16.zh:
當下摩西急切地尋找作贖罪祭的公山羊，誰知已經焚燒了，便向亞倫剩下的兒子以利亞撒、以他瑪發怒，說：

**摩西急切地尋找。**摩西仍在關注是否一切都按上帝的吩咐執行。在獻山羊為贖罪祭時，血不得帶進聖所，而是抹在燔祭壇的四角上。根據條例，在這種情況下，肉應由祭司吃掉（利6:26）。那一天，曾獻上一隻山羊為贖罪祭（利9:15）。由於血沒有帶進聖所，肉就應該吃掉。但卻沒有這樣做。那就大大損害了這件崇事的象徵意義。
亞倫沒有吃那肉，所以不能承擔百姓的罪孽。他無法為他沒有承擔的罪進行贖罪。這就使錯誤顯得更加嚴重。山羊所擔當的罪孽應當轉移給為之贖罪的祭司。但這一次罪沒有轉移，因為祭司沒有吃那肉。山羊所能做的就是死。但代求的工作仍有待完成。
**便向……發怒。**摩西是以謙和著稱的（民12:3），但他仍會發義怒。他曾義憤填膺，把兩塊石版摔碎，但上帝並沒有因此而責怪他（出32:19）。上帝自己也很生氣（出32:9,10）。摩西的忿怒沒有消退，因為當他看見金牛犢時，他將它磨碎並讓以色列人喝那水（出32:20）。
有時是需要把義憤表達出來的。這時無疑要遵循保羅的教導：“生氣卻不要犯罪”（弗4:26）。保羅論到自己說：“有誰跌倒，我不焦急呢？”（林後11:29）。當保羅看見別人受到虐待時，他就非常義憤。“焦急”的原文是“著火”。當摩西摔碎石版時，他“便發烈怒”。亞倫為此而責備他（出32:19,22），覺得沒有什麼值得生氣的。但正如前面所指出的，耶和華與摩西都認為發怒是有正當理由的。他的怒氣是出於他對上帝和祂聖工的熱忱，而不是出於個人的驕傲或報復心。

17.zh:
這贖罪祭既是至聖的，主又給了你們，為要你們擔當會眾的罪孽，在耶和華面前為他們贖罪，你們為何沒有在聖所吃呢？

**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》418；《先祖與先知》354。

19.zh:
亞倫對摩西說：今天他們在耶和華面前獻上贖罪祭和燔祭，我又遇見這樣的災，若今天吃了贖罪祭，耶和華豈能看為美呢？

雖然摩西是對亞倫的兒子以利亞撒和以他瑪說話，並責備他們，但回答的卻是他們的父親。亞倫知道吃贖罪祭象徵承擔獻祭者的罪，正如摩西所說的。但由於所發生的事情，以及他自身的部分責任，他覺得他不能承擔他人的罪。他只能承擔自己的罪。他正為兒子的死而悲傷，甚至可能有一點怨恨。他顯然認為按他目前的心情，他作為預表性的承擔罪孽者是不會蒙上帝悅納的。

20.zh:
摩西聽見這話，便以為美。

也可譯為“滿意”，“高興”。摩西看到亞倫沒有疏忽大意，也沒有無故忽略已知的職責。他接受了亞倫的解釋，並相應地改變了自己的態度。

9.en: Wash in water. In harmony with the rule that nothing unclean must come on the altar or be used in the service of God, the entrails and the legs were washed in water before the victim was placed on the altar. It might readily be argued that this was unnecessary, as the fire would soon consume the sacrifice and everything unclean be destroyed. Why, then, spend time in washing parts of the animal? This, again, must have deeply impressed all with the holiness of God, and His hatred of disorder and everything that defiles. In fact, every act, every ceremony, brought home the lesson of the sacredness of God’s work, the holiness of His character. The priest shall burn all. There was one exception to this: the skin was not burned, but given to the priest (ch. 7:8). We are not told why this exception was made. A sweet savour. That is, pleasing to Him. The burnt offerings of ch. 1 were not mandatory offerings but voluntary, something the offerer brought because he felt his need of God and wanted to show his appreciation for the goodness of the Lord. In bringing the offering he was expressing his love for God and consecrating himself to His service. Burnt offerings were offered on many occasions and represented consecration and thankfulness to God. They did not call for any specific favor, but expressed gratitude for past mercies. They were offered in the cleansing of a leper (ch. 14:19, 20), the cleansing of women after childbirth (ch. 12:6–8), and also for general defilement (ch. 15:15, 30). In many cases a sin offering accompanied the burnt offering, but not always. When sin and burnt offerings were brought by the same individual, the sin offering came first and was for a specific sin or sins; the burnt offering was for general sinfulness, without reference to any particular sin. Burnt offerings had a prominent place in the consecration of Aaron and his sons (Ex. 29:15–25; Lev. 8:18), as well as their induction into the priesthood (Lev. 9:12–14). They were also used in Nazirite vows (Num. 6:13–16). In these instances they stood for complete consecration of the individual to God. In them the offerer placed himself symbolically on the altar, his life wholly devoted to God’s service. Sacrifices were embodied prayers. Considered in this light they take on deeper meaning. If a Christian falls into temptation and commits a sin, he meekly confesses his sin and asks for forgiveness. The true Israelite did the same, but in addition he brought a sin offering for the specific sin. If he also brought a burnt offering, he was in that act saying, “Lord, I may have done other things also that are not pleasing to Thee. I am not aware that I have done this, but in mercy forgive wherein I may have come short.” When we pray this prayer today we are doing what the Israelite did when he brought his burnt offering. Paul’s expression in Rom. 12:1, “present your bodies a living sacrifice,” is a reference to ancient burnt offerings. We are to be wholly dedicated to God. We are to be completely cleansed. Only when all filth was removed from the burnt offering, was it permitted to come upon the altar, “an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the Lord.” So it is with us. All sin, all filthiness of the flesh and of the spirit, must be removed before we are fit for the altar (2 Cor. 7:1). The burnt offering is a type of Christ, who gave Himself fully, completely to God, leaving an example for us to follow. It teaches entire sanctification, complete dedication. It is rightly placed first in the list of offerings in Leviticus. It tells us in no uncertain tones that to be a sweet savor unto God, a sacrifice must be one of entire surrender. All must be placed on the altar, all must be dedicated to God. As the sacrifice was to be perfect, so Christ is the “lamb without blemish and without spot,” the One altogether lovely, the Holy One, who “loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour” (1 Peter 1:19; Eph. 5:2). The burnt sacrifice was pleasing to God because it revealed a desire in the heart of the offerer to dedicate himself to God. In bringing his sacrifice the offerer said in effect, “Lord, I desire to serve Thee. I am placing myself on the altar, reserving nothing for myself. Accept me in the Substitute and for His sake.” Such an attitude is pleasing to God. The burnt offerings of ch. 1 were a “sweet savour” unto God because they were entirely voluntary. Christians are in danger of doing that which in itself is good and right, not because of an inner urge or an impelling love but because it is the custom or because it is expected. Duty is a great word and should be emphasized; but we are not to forget that love is still greater, and that rightly applied it fulfills duty because it includes duty. Love is voluntary, spontaneous, free; duty is exacting, compulsory. Both are necessary in the Christian life, and one must not be stressed to the exclusion of the other. Duty fulfills the law and goes all the way. Love also fulfills the law and goes all the way; but then it goes even further. It goes the second mile. It gives the cloak also. “God loveth a cheerful giver” (2 Cor. 9:7). Some would substitute “liberal” for “cheerful” which would probably be true also. But the text reads “cheerful.” It denotes one who gives willingly, who does not need to be urged, but cheerfully does his part. Such is pleasing to God. This spirit is typified in the burnt offering. It would be pleasing to God if the spirit of happy, cheerful service were more common than it is. Often we do resignedly, perhaps even with grumbling, that which we should do with eagerness and a happy spirit. God loves a cheerful giver, not only of money but of service. There are tasks to be done that are not agreeable or pleasant. God appreciates our doing them as a matter of duty, but He would be even more pleased if we would do them voluntarily and without murmur or complaint. There are those who have to be encouraged, admonished, urged, almost bribed to do what they should do cheerfully and of their own free will (see Isa. 64:7; Mal. 1:10). An indifferent attitude and the desire for reward weary both men and God. It is disheartening to leaders to admonish earnestly and repeatedly and win but a feeble response.
9.zh:
但燔祭的臟腑與腿要用水洗。祭司就要把一切全燒在壇上，當作燔祭，獻與耶和華為馨香的火祭。

**用水洗。**凡不潔淨之物都不得擺在壇上或用在上帝的崇事中。所以在祭牲擺在壇上之前，內臟和腿都要在水中洗乾淨。可能會有人說這沒有必要，因為火很快會燒盡祭物，而一切不潔淨的東西都會燒掉。何必再化時間洗祭牲的各部分呢？
這一定又是為使眾人深刻認識上帝的聖潔，以及祂對混亂和一切汙穢之物的憎惡。事實上每一舉措和禮節都體現了上帝工作的神聖，及其品格的聖潔。
**祭司就要把一切全燒。**除了皮以外。皮要給祭司（利7:8）。聖經沒有告訴我們原因。
**馨香的。**這是令祂喜愛的。第1章的燔祭不是必獻的，而是出於自願的，是獻祭者感到他需要上帝，要表示他感激耶和華的良善。他藉著獻祭表達了他對上帝的愛，並獻身為祂服務。
在許多場合下都獻燔祭，表示對上帝的獻身和感恩。獻這些祭並不要求得到任何特別的恩惠，只是表達對以往仁慈的感激。如在大麻風患者的潔淨（利14:19,20）、婦人生子的潔淨（利12:6-8）以及一般汙穢的潔淨（利15:15,30）時要獻燔祭。在許多情況下，贖罪祭和燔祭一起獻，但並非總是如此。當贖罪祭和燔祭由同一個人獻上時，要先獻贖罪祭，為了一個或多個特定的罪；燔祭是為籠統的罪，而不是為特定的罪奉獻的。
燔祭在亞倫和他的兒子承接聖職之禮（出29:15-25；利8:18），以及他們就任祭司職分之禮中（利9:12-14）具有顯著的地位。它們還用在還拿細耳人的願時（民6:13-16）。在這些情形下，它們象徵了個人向上帝完全的獻身。獻祭者象徵性地將自己擺在壇上，將他的生命完全奉獻為上帝服務。
獻祭是祈禱的具體表現。從這一角度來看，它們具有更深刻的意義。如果一個基督徒陷入試探並且犯罪，他就謙卑地認罪並請求饒恕。真以色列人也是如此行的，但除此以外，他還為特定的罪獻上了一個贖罪祭。如果他又獻上一個燔祭，那麼他就是藉此說：“耶和華啊！我可能做了其他的事情也令你不愉快。我沒有意識到我做了這樣的事，但求你憑仁慈饒恕我在那方面的虧欠”。當我們今日這樣的禱告時，我們乃是在做以色列人獻燔祭時所做的事情。
保羅在羅12:1節中所說“將身體獻上，當作活祭”，指的就是古代的燔祭。我們應當完全地獻身給上帝，完全地被潔淨。只有除去祭物的一切汙穢，它才可出以現在壇上，“獻與耶和華為馨香的火祭”。我們也當如此。一切的罪、一切肉體和心靈的汙穢都必須去除，然後才配得上祭壇（林後7:1）。
燔祭是基督的預表。祂完全地將自己獻給上帝，為我們留下了效法的榜樣。燔祭教導我們完全的成聖，完全的獻身。把燔祭列在《利未記》各種祭祀之首是十分恰當的。它清楚地告訴我們，要獻與耶和華為馨香的火祭，祭物必須完全獻上。一切都必須擺在壇上，獻給上帝。
正如祭物應是完全的，基督也是那“無瑕疵、無玷汙的羔羊”，全然可愛的主，“愛我們，為我們舍了自己，當作馨香的供物和祭物，獻與上帝”的聖者（彼前1:19；弗5:2）。
燔祭是上帝所喜悅的，因為它表達了獻祭者獻身上帝的心願。他在獻祭時實際上是在說：“耶和華啊！我願意服侍你。我將自己毫無保留地擺在壇上。請因替罪之主的緣故而接納我吧”。這樣的態度是上帝所喜悅的。
利1章中的燔祭是獻與上帝“馨香的供物”，因為它們完全是自願的。基督徒有這樣一種危險，就是他們行善不是因為內在的願望或愛心，而是根據習慣或責任。責任是高尚的；但我們不要忘記愛是更高尚的。正確地運用愛心就是履行了責任，因為它包括了責任。愛是自願的、自發的、自由的；責任是嚴格要求的、強制性的。兩者都是基督徒人生中不可少的，不可厚此薄彼。責任成全律法而且起到自己的作用。愛也成全律法並起到自己的作用；但愛的作用更大。它會走第二里路。連外衣也會佈施。
“捐得樂意的人是上帝所喜愛的”（林後9:7）。有些人喜歡用“慷慨”來代替“樂意”，這可能也是正確的。但“樂意”表示甘心給予，不需要催促，樂意儘自己職責的人。這是上帝所喜悅的。燔祭象徵了這種精神。現在若有更多樂意服務的精神，那將會蒙上帝所喜悅。我們經常被動地，甚至帶著怨言去做我們本應熱心和高興去做的事情。上帝喜愛捐得樂意的人，不僅是指金錢而且包括服務。有些需要完成的任務不是令人愉快的或可愛的。上帝賞識我們把這些工作當作責任。但如果我們毫無怨言地自願去做這些事的話，祂會更加高興。有些人須在受到鼓勵、勸勉、要求、甚至幾乎是物質刺激的情況下，才肯做他們本應甘心樂意去做的事情（見賽64:7；瑪1:10）。麻木的態度和渴望賞賜的慾望使人和上帝都感到厭煩。誠懇而反覆的勸勉只得到微弱的回應，這會使領袖十分沮喪。

5.en: Kill the bullock. We cannot believe that a normal individual would take pleasure in plunging a knife into an innocent victim, even though that victim be only an animal. Yet God required this act of the offerer. In later times the priests did the slaying, thought it was God’s original intent that the sinner himself should do so. This must have been a painful and distressing experience for the sinner, because he knew that it was his sin that made the death necessary. It must have impressed him with the determination to “go, and sin no more.” He saw vividly before him the result of sin. It meant not only death, but the death of an innocent one. What other result could this ceremony have than to create in the transgressor a hatred for sin and a solemn resolve to have no more to do with it? The first lesson God wanted to teach Israel through the sacrificial system was that sin means death. Again and again this lesson was impressed upon their hearts. Every morning and evening throughout the year a lamb was offered for the nation. Day after day the people brought their sin offerings and their burnt offerings to the sanctuary. In each case an animal was slain and the blood ministered in the appointed place. On every ceremony and on every service was stamped the lesson: Sin means death. This lesson is needed as much in our time as it was in the days of old. Some Christians hold sin too lightly. They think of it as a passing aspect of life that mankind will outgrow. Others consider sin regrettable but unavoidable. All need to have impressed indelibly upon the mind the lesson that sin means death. The NT specifically states that “the wages of sin is death” (Rom. 6:23), but many fail to grasp the importance of the statement. A more realistic conception of sin and death as being inseparably connected would help much in an appreciation and understanding of the gospel. For the Christian this holds an important lesson. We were guilty, not He. A contemplation of the cross should bring to us first a feeling of guilt, then of revulsion from sin, and finally profound thankfulness to God that through death comes salvation. Christ died for me. I should have died, for I sinned, and “the wages of sin is death.” But Christ died for me; He went to Calvary in my place! How adequate the provision! How wonderful the love! Sprinkle the blood. The offerer had finished his work. He had brought his sacrifice, confessed his sin, and slain the victim. Now the ministration of the blood began. A priest had stood by as the blood gushed forth, and had caught it in a vessel. He now ministered the blood by sprinkling it round about upon the altar of burnt offering. The word here translated “sprinkle” literally means “to scatter.” It is used of scattering dust (Job 2:12), live coals (Eze. 10:2), water (Num. 19:13), etc. According to the Talmud the officiating priest scattered the blood against the altar at two places, the northeastern and southwestern corners, in such a way that it would touch all four sides of the altar. For sanitary reasons this was probably done on the inside of the altar. The unused portion of the blood was poured out at the bottom of the altar. Later, at the Temple in Jerusalem, surplus blood was disposed of by means of a tile drain, which conveyed it to the brook Kidron. God sought to impress upon Israel that forgiveness of sin can be obtained only through confession and the ministration of blood. They were to realize the infinite cost of forgiveness. It is more than merely overlooking faults. It cost God something to be able to forgive; it cost a life, even the life of His own Son. To some the death of Christ appears unnecessary. God could, or should, they think, forgive without Calvary. The cross does not seem to them an integral and vital part of the atonement. It would be well if Christians today contemplated more than they do the cost of their salvation. Forgiveness is not a simple matter. Through the ceremonial system God taught Israel that forgiveness can be had only through the shedding of blood. We need that lesson now. In the sacrificial system of Israel are to be found the fundamental principles of holy living. The OT is fundamental. He who is thoroughly grounded in it will be able to erect a superstructure that will not fall when the rains descend and the winds blow. He will be “built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone” (Eph. 2:20).
5.zh:
他要在耶和華面前宰公牛；亞倫子孫作祭司的，要奉上血，把血灑在會幕門口、壇的周圍。

**宰公牛。**我們無法相信一個正常的人會喜歡將一把刀刺入一個無辜的受害者體內，即或只是一隻動物。但上帝卻要求獻祭者採取這樣的舉動。在以後的時代中，祭司承接了宰殺的工作，儘管上帝起初的意圖是讓罪人自己如此行。這對於罪人來說一定是一種痛苦而煩惱的經驗，因為他知道正是他的罪造成死亡。這一定使他痛下決心“從此不再犯罪了”。他親眼看見了罪的後果。這不僅意味著死亡，而且意味著無辜者的死亡。除了在犯罪的人心中產生一種對罪的恨惡和不再犯罪的莊嚴決心之外，這一禮儀還能產生什麼其他的結果呢？
上帝藉著獻祭的制度首先要教導以色列人的，就是罪意味著死亡。這一教訓一次又一次地銘刻在他們的心上。一年到頭，每天早晚都有一隻羊羔為全民族而被獻上。百姓日復一日地將他們的贖罪祭和燔祭帶到聖所來。在每一情形中，都有一隻祭牲被宰殺，都有血被塗抹在指定的地方。在每一禮儀和崇事中都銘刻著這樣一個教訓：罪意味著死亡。
現代象古時一樣都需要這一教訓。有些基督徒對罪不當回事。他們認為罪只是人生短暫的階段，會隨著人類的成長而消失的。其他的人則認為罪雖可懊悔但不可避免。每個基督徒都需要牢牢記住罪意味著死亡的教訓。新約聖經特別說明“罪的工價乃是死”（羅6:23），但許多人卻未能領悟這句話的重要性。我們只有更加清楚地認識到罪和死亡密不可分的聯繫，才能欣賞和理解福音的真理。對於基督徒而言，這包含著一個重要的教訓。有罪的是我們，而不是祂。我們默想十字架，首先將產生一種負罪感，然後是對罪的厭惡，最終無限感激上帝使救恩因死亡而臨到我們。基督為我而死。該死的本應是我，因我犯了罪，而“罪的工價乃是死”。但基督為我死了；祂替我去了髑髏地！上帝的預備是何等的充足！上帝的愛是何等的奇妙！
**把血灑在。**獻祭者已完成了他的工作。他已帶來了祭物，認了罪，宰了祭牲。現在灑血的儀式開始了。當鮮血湧出時，一個祭司準備著將血接在一個器皿裡。他現在將血灑在燔祭壇的周圍。“灑”可用來指散塵土（伯2:12），火炭（結10:2）和水（民19:13）等。根據《塔木德》的記載，司儀的祭司把血灑向壇的東北角和西南角，這樣就能沾到壇的四邊。出於衛生的原因，這很可能是灑在壇的內側。未用過的血被倒在壇的底下。後來，在耶路撒冷的聖殿中，多餘的血藉助一個用瓦片砌成的下水道排走，流到汲淪溪。
上帝要使以色列認識到，只有藉著認罪和灑血才能獲得赦罪。他們應意識到饒恕的無限代價。這不僅是不計較過錯。上帝付出了相當大的代價才能施行饒恕。這代價乃是一條性命，甚至是祂親生兒子的性命。
有些人覺得基督的死是不必要的。他們認為上帝無需髑髏地就能實施饒恕。十字架對他們來說似乎不是贖罪的一個重要部分。巴不得今日的基督徒能更多地思考他們得救的代價。饒恕不是一件簡單的事情。藉著儀文的制度，上帝教導以色列人，饒恕只能藉著流血才能得到。我們現今也需要這樣的教訓。在以色列人的獻祭制度中可以找到聖潔生活的基本原則。舊約聖經是至關重要的。凡徹底地紮根在其上的人，都能建造起不怕風吹雨打的建築。他將“被建造在使徒和先知的根基上，有基督耶穌自己為房角石”（弗2:20）。

8.en: Lay the parts. The lesson of orderliness is the same as in v. 7. All parts of the victim were to be placed in position on the altar as in the living animal, on the wood which was also “in order.” Says the apostle, “Let all things be done decently and in order” (1 Cor. 14:40). This is good NT Christianity.
8.zh:
亞倫子孫作祭司的，要把肉塊和頭並脂油擺在壇上火的柴上。

有關次序的教訓與第7節中的相同。祭牲的所有部分都要象活的動物那樣按照適當的位置被擺在壇的柴上。柴也是擺放整齊的。使徒說：“凡事都要規規矩矩地按著次序行”（林前14:40）。這是新約基督教的重要教義。

6.en: Flay the burnt offering. Originally, the offerer himself did this, though this part of the ritual was later taken over by the Levites. In the wilderness there were but few to participate in the services, as compared with later times, in the Promised Land, when hundreds and even thousands of offerers arrived in a single day. The Levites and priests who were accustomed to the ritual could perform the flaying more expeditiously than the people.
6.zh:
那人要剝去燔祭牲的皮，把燔祭牲切成塊子。

儘管儀式的這一部分後來由利未人接手，但起初獻祭者要親自動手。在曠野中，只有很少的人參與這些崇事，而後來到了應許之地，一天就有成百上千的獻祭者來到。專門從事這些儀式的利未人和祭司剝皮的動作比百姓要快。

7.en: Put fire upon the altar. At a designated place upon the altar of burnt offering a fire was always burning. It was the duty of the priests to make sure that this fire never went out. Because God Himself had kindled it, it was considered sacred fire. This fire must not be put to common use, nor must common fire be used in any sanctuary service. From this central fire on the altar, the priests lighted other fires to accommodate such sacrifices as might be brought. Thus several fires were burning at the altar at one time, all lighted from the one central fire. It was from this altar that the priests took coals for their censers when they went in to offer incense in the holy place. The fire on the altar of incense came from the altar of burnt offering. It is interesting to note that in heaven there is an angel who has charge of the fire (Rev. 14:18). Lay the wood in order. The wood used in the sanctuary service was carefully inspected before it was permitted to come on the altar. Wood that had been attacked by insects or eaten by worms was rejected. It was the work of certain of the priests to provide and care for the wood, and once a year the people were asked to help gather fuel for the sanctuary. This must in itself have been educational for them; for as they gathered the wood and examined it to see that it would pass the inspection of the priests, they must have been impressed with God’s holiness and His demand for perfection even in small matters. The wood was not thrown on the fire, nor casually put on. It was carefully placed “in order.” The lesson is evident. Nothing that has to do with God’s service may be done in a slipshod manner. All must be done with care and reverence.
7.zh:
祭司亞倫的子孫要把火放在壇上，把柴擺在火上。

**把火放在壇上。**在燔祭壇上一個指定的地方總是有火燒著。保證這火永不熄滅乃是祭司的職責。因為上帝親自點燃了它。它被視為聖火。這火絕不得用在俗事上。凡火也不得被用在聖所的任何崇事中。祭司從這壇中央的火點燃了其他的火，來接受可能獻上的祭物。這樣，在壇上會同時有許多火燃燒，都是從一箇中央的火點燃的。祭司在進入聖所獻香時就是從這壇上取香爐所需的火炭的。香壇上的火也來自燔祭壇。值得注意的是在天上也有一位天使有權柄管火（啟14:18）。
**把柴擺在火上。**在聖所崇事中所使用的柴，在放上祭壇之前要仔細檢查。被蟲蛀或咬過的柴要丟棄。有些祭司的工作就是提供和照看木柴的。百姓有義務一年一度幫助收集聖所所需的燃料。這對他們來說一定是具有教育意義的。因為當他們收集柴火併察看它是否會通過祭司的檢查時，他們一定對上帝的聖潔和祂甚至對微小事物所要求的完美留下深刻的印象。
柴不是仍進火裡，也不是隨便地放上。而是小心“擺”上的。這教訓是顯而易見的。凡與上帝的崇事有關的事，都不許以一種草率的方式來做。一切都必須小心而恭敬地完成。

1.zh:
耶和華從會幕中呼叫摩西，對他說：

上帝曾應許在會幕建立後，祂將在聖所中與摩西交往。祂從前曾在山上對他說話，但現在祂要在施恩座上說話（出25:22）。祂現在實現這一應許，呼叫摩西前來，以便通過他來指教百姓如何接近上帝和聖所。
這種指示是非常需要的。以色列人對上帝的聖潔和罪的邪惡本質認識不清。需要指教百姓恭敬與崇拜的首要原則。他們要懂得不僅上帝是聖潔的，祂的居所甚至其周圍的事物都是神聖的。他們要懂得人非聖潔就不能接近上帝，來到祂的面前。他們不可擅自闖入上帝的居所，最多隻能到院子的門口，懷著謙卑和痛悔的心來獻祭。祭司們將替上帝從他們手中接過祭物，並在聖所裡獻血和燒香。就連祭司都不能進入至聖所主持崇事。這隻留給了大祭司。他在深刻地省察己心之後才能一年一次在贖罪大日進入至聖所待幾分鐘。然後至聖所又將保持關閉一年之久。上帝確實是至聖的。
藉著被殺的羊羔；藉著公牛、公綿羊、公山羊、斑鳩、雛鴿；藉著灑血在燔祭壇上、在香壇上、彈血在幔子上、或在約櫃上；藉著祭司的教訓和代求，以色列人應學會如何接近上帝，在面對上帝神聖律法的定罪時不至被撇在無助的境地之中。他們有一條逃生之路。上帝的羔羊將為他們而死。藉著對其寶血的信心，他們得以與上帝建立親密的交往。藉著祭司的代求，他們以祭司為代表得以進入聖所，甚至以大祭司為代表來到至高者的臺前。對於忠心的以色列人來說，這預表著上帝的百姓“因耶穌的血得以坦然進入至聖所”的時候（來10:19）。
上帝希望藉著獻祭的制度將這一切教導以色列人。這是他們的得救之道，給予了他們希望和勇氣。儘管上帝十誡的律法定了他們的罪，但上帝的羔羊要為他們而死的事實，卻給了他們希望。獻祭的制度成了以色列人的福音。它指明與上帝交往的路徑。
有些自稱為基督徒的人看不出上帝所指定的聖殿崇事對他們有什麼重要性或價值。然而通過了解《舊約》，《新約》中救贖的福音計劃會顯得更為清晰。事實上，凡明白《舊約》中獻祭制度的人，能夠更好地理解並欣賞《新約》中所闡明的福音真理。前者預示著後者，是後者的一種預表。
**從會幕中。**人類因為犯罪從其樂園中被趕了出來。他在那樂園中曾享受與創造主暢通無阻的交往。由於人再也不配與上帝一同生活，所以上帝現在屈尊下來與人一同生活。祂指示摩西說：“又當為我造聖所，使我可以住在他們中間”（出25:8）。摩西執行了。“耶和華的榮光充滿了帳幕”（出40:34）。何等奇妙的愛！上帝無法忍受與祂自己的子民隔絕。祂憑愛心設計出了一個計劃，使祂可以依然與他們生活在一起！祂願意和他們在曠野飄流的路途中同行，並最終領他們進入應許之地。

2.zh:
你曉諭以色列人說：你們中間若有人獻供物給耶和華，要從牛群羊群中獻牲畜為供物。

供物（qorban），源於動詞qarab（“靠近”、“接近”）。燔祭有兩種：法定的和自願的。某些法定的燔祭是在指定的時間由祭司替全民族而獻上的，包括每日當獻的燔祭（出29:38-42；民28:3-8），安息日當獻的燔祭（民28:9,10），在月朔、逾越節、五旬節、吹角節、贖罪日和住棚節所獻的，節期當獻的燔祭（民28:11至29:39）。其他法定的燔祭屬於臨時性的，並由個人所獻，包括在祭司接受聖職之禮時（出29:15-18；利8:18-21；9:12-14），在生子時（利12:6-8），在行對大麻風患者的潔淨之禮時（利14:19,20），在潔淨儀文的汙穢時（利15:14,15,30），以及在還拿細耳人的願時（民6:13-16）所獻的燔祭。自願的燔祭可以由個人在任何時候獻上，但必須符合法定燔祭的各方面規定的各方面（見民7；王上8:64）。利1章中的規定特別針對自願的燔祭，儘管其儀式也與其他的相似。

3.zh:
他的供物若以牛為燔祭，就要在會幕門口獻一隻沒有殘疾的公牛，可以在耶和華面前蒙悅納。

**他的供物若以牛為燔祭。**“燔祭” ，希伯來語是`Olah，指“上去的”或“上升的”。另一個表示“燔祭”的詞是kalil，僅用過兩次，意思是“全”。這些詞彙表示燔祭完全在壇上焚燒；隨著煙往上冒，祭物也象徵性地上升到上帝那裡。燔祭的任何部分都不得像其他祭物的某些部分那樣吃掉；一切都要被燒在火中作為“馨香的火祭”升到上帝那裡（第9節）。任何東西都不得保留。一切都要獻給上帝。這表示完全的奉獻。
燔祭是在洪水之後首次提到的，那時挪亞“在壇上獻燔祭”（創8:20）。燔祭在上帝對亞伯拉罕所說“在我所要指示你的山上”獻子“為燔祭”的吩咐中再次提到（創22:2）。《約伯記》可能是聖經最古老的著作，其中記載了約伯“清早起來，……獻燔祭；因為他說：‘恐怕我兒子犯了罪，心中棄掉上帝’”（伯1:5）。約伯顯然相信他的燔祭有利於避免上帝的忿怒，即或他的兒子沒有為自己獻任何的祭物，甚至可能沒有意識到他們犯了罪。拉比有一句常話說：“燔祭為以色列人的過犯贖罪”。
燔祭是所有獻祭中最早的形式，而且是最有特色和最全面的獻祭形式，它綜合了所有獻祭的基本要素。這是數百年來僅存的獻祭形式，說明了其重要性。後來主吩咐獻其他祭時，清楚地說明它們不應取代而應補充“常獻的燔祭”（見民28:10；29:16等）。
每日早晚的獻祭在贖罪日也不例外。雖然它是為了整個民族，但也適合於每一個以色列人的需要。當聖所的崇事最終在耶路撒冷建立起來時，上帝吩咐說從此以後所有的祭都應在那裡獻，只有祭司才可以在壇旁司儀。這雖然有使敬拜集中並趨於統一的好處，但卻給那些遠離聖所的人帶來困難。從加利利到耶路撒冷的路程需要好幾天，特別是帶著祭牲的話。在回家的路上，那人可能會再次犯罪而又需要回去獻祭。這當然造成了一種不可能解決的難題。為此，每日早晚的獻祭提供了一個令人滿意的解決方案。
每日崇事中規定要用的祭牲是用全民捐助的錢買來的。每天清早，一隻羊羔為全民族而被獻在燔祭壇上，在黃昏，此崇事被重複。燔祭為民族提供了一種臨時性的贖罪，直到罪人能夠親自到場獻上他自己的祭物時為止。這些全國性的獻祭對民族所起的作用和約伯在說：“恐怕我兒子犯了罪，心中棄掉上帝”時所抱的想法一樣（伯1:5）。約伯並不知道他的兒子是否犯了罪。但他們有可能犯了罪。所以為了“遮掩”他們直到他們獻上他們自己的祭物為止，約伯就為他們而行。同樣，每日為全國所獻的燔祭遮掩以色列人的罪，直到每個人能獻上他個人的祭物為止。《塔木德》教訓說，早祭為晚上犯的罪贖罪，晚祭為白天犯的罪贖罪。
每日當獻的燔祭被燒在壇上，但須在慢火之上，以便使一次祭可以持續到下一次獻祭的時候（利6:9）。晚祭要持續到清早，早祭要持續到黃昏。這樣始終有一個祭牲在壇上為以色列民提供暫時性的贖罪。當一個人犯了罪時，他雖然無法立刻，甚至在幾周或幾個月之內，來到聖所，但他知道在壇上有一個祭物為他而獻。他被“遮掩”直到他能帶他自己的祭物來確認他的悔改為止。
這個為古時罪人制定的仁慈規定，成為今日罪人的可靠盼望。有時我們犯了罪，但到後來才意識到，因此沒有立即認罪。基督始終願意用祂的義袍“遮掩”我們，直到我們意識到我們的景況為止。祂永不離棄我們。在我們來到祂面前之前祂就為我們的救恩做了必要的準備。這給我們帶來何等大的安慰啊！感謝上帝這樣奇妙的恩賜！但任何人都不應濫用這一優惠而耽延認罪。
利1章中所談到的個人燔祭雖然都是自願的，但如前所述，在獻祭的時候，所應遵照的儀式仍是精確而嚴格的。以色列人如此懂得了絕對的順從。上帝可以饒恕，上帝也願意饒恕，但必須絕對服從上帝的指令。凡要靠近上帝的人必須按照上帝所指定的方式。只有按照祂的旨意敬拜，才能被祂所接受。不是按照我們覺得最好和最有效的方式，也不是我們所認為最適宜的方式，更不是看起來會帶來最快的回報或最多金錢的方式，而只能是上帝所認可並能賜福的方式。
用作燔祭的有四種動物：公牛、綿羊、山羊、鳥。獻祭者可以隨意選擇其中的一種。買得起公牛的有錢人自然會帶一隻牛來。只能買得起一隻斑鳩或雛鴿的窮人會帶其中的一隻來。值得一提的是，耶穌的母親瑪利亞帶了兩隻斑鳩來到聖殿作為她生子後所獻的禮物（見利12:8；路2:22-24）。約瑟和瑪利亞都是窮人。獸類和鳥類中的君王獅子和老鷹作為不潔淨的動物，沒有被用在獻祭中，所用的卻是羊羔和鴿子。上帝不理睬高傲、傲慢的精神，而接受柔和謙卑的人。
自願獻的燔祭是一種出於愛心，歸主為聖的禮物。這是在樂意犧牲的精神下獻給上帝的。這不僅僅是一種禮物，而是以自己為活祭。我們今日不再獻燔祭，但我們卻可以將激發人獻燔祭的精神應用在基督徒生活的每一天中。上帝喜愛甘心樂意的服務（林後9:7）。
**一隻沒有殘疾的公牛。**“所獻的必純全無殘疾的，才蒙悅納”（利22:21）。這強調上帝要我們最好的東西。我們可能並不富有，不能將重禮獻給上帝，但我們所給的必須是完全的。我們不應將任何次要的東西獻上。我們不應獻給上帝低值的東西──一個有瑕疵的錢幣、滯銷的財產、一點空閒的時間。我們應當以所能支配的最佳事物服侍上帝。

4.zh:
他要按手在燔祭牲的頭上，燔祭便蒙悅納，為他贖罪。

所獻祭牲被視為罪人的替身。它應“為他”得蒙悅納。由於這個替身是基督的一種預表，所以必須是完全的（利22:25）。
此儀式的一個嚴肅的重要部分就是獻祭者按手在祭牲頭上。Samak（“按”）一詞的意思就是用自身的重量“倚靠”，一種悔罪的罪人表示對替身完全依賴的動作。這一舉動的含義，古代和現代的註釋家都知道是象徵著獻祭者的罪轉到祭牲身上，或象徵祭牲代替罪人而死。“按手在祭牲的頭上乃是一種平常的儀式，藉以使罪的替代和轉移生效”。“在每一次獻祭中都有替罪的概念；祭牲代替了罪人”（《猶太教百科全書》第2冊第286頁，標題“贖罪日”）。
基督徒現在因信將他們的罪歸在上帝的羔羊耶穌身上，所以在獻祭的崇事中完全能找到預表這一點的禮儀，這就是燔祭的儀式所反映的。事實上，按手在一切涉及到罪的情況中，都是必不可少的。基督徒從按手和倚靠在祭牲身上的禮儀中，看出這預表他自己靠賴基督而得救。在這樣的靠賴中，我們將自己的罪放在祂的身上，祂在祭壇上代替我們，成為“聖潔的，是上帝所喜悅”的祭（羅12:1）。
悔過的罪人按照上帝所吩咐的去做，就可以確知那祭牲已代替他而蒙悅納了。我們也是如此。當我們遵守上帝的吩咐時，我們也可以確知自己在替罪者基督裡已蒙悅納了。祂在祭壇上代替了我們──祂事實上已經在十字架上如此做了。祂為我們而死，替我們而死，我們因祂的死而得以存活。

10.zh:
人的供物若以綿羊或山羊為燔祭，就要獻上沒有殘疾的公羊。

如果獻祭者負擔不起或不想獻公牛，他可以從羊群中選擇一隻綿羊或山羊。這是上帝所能悅納的；但不論他選什麼，都必須是一隻公的，而且是無殘疾的。

11.zh:
要把羊宰於壇的北邊，在耶和華面前；亞倫子孫作祭司的，要把羊血灑在壇的周圍。

與獻公牛的儀式一樣。這裡沒有提按手在祭牲頭上，但肯定有按手。和獻公牛一樣，祭司準備接血並將血灑在壇的周圍（見第5節注）。

13.zh:
但臟腑與腿要用水洗，祭司就要全然奉獻，燒在壇上。這是燔祭，是獻與耶和華為馨香的火祭。

這裡與獻公牛的程序一樣。祭牲被剝皮，切成塊子，腿和內臟洗淨，然後各部分拿到壇上擺放整齊。

14.zh:
人奉給耶和華的供物，若以鳥為燔祭，就要獻斑鳩或是雛鴿為供物。

斑鳩和雛鴿十分便宜，窮人也獻得起。應當記住利1章中的供物都是自願的。但一顆充滿了愛的心總會設法將一件禮物獻給上帝，不論它多麼微小。這樣的供物在上帝看來和那些大的供物一樣貴重。
耶穌在談到投兩個小錢的寡婦時，清楚地教導了這一道理，說她“所投的比眾人還多”（路21:3,4）。一個小錢的禮物的確是非常之小。但她卻獻出了她的一切。所奉獻的不在於她給了多少，而在於她還剩下多少。

15.zh:
祭司要把鳥拿到壇前，揪下頭來，把鳥燒在壇上；鳥的血要流在壇的旁邊；

通常要獻祭者自己動手宰殺。但鳥的血量很少，所以需祭司親自宰殺，以便迅速地用血抹祭壇。

16.zh:
又要把鳥的嗉子和髒物（髒物：或作翎毛）除掉，丟在壇的東邊倒灰的地方。

丟在灰堆上，是因為燃燒會產生難聞的氣味。

17.zh:
要拿著鳥的兩個翅膀，把鳥撕開，只是不可撕斷；祭司要在壇上、在火的柴上焚燒。這是燔祭，是獻與耶和華為馨香的火祭。

鳥太小而無法被分割，象對其他祭牲那樣灑血和按手（見第4節注）；但它們仍是獻與上帝的馨香之物。獻祭者除了提供鳥以外，無須插手此儀式。祭司包攬剩下的一切。儘管如此，獻祭者已盡了自己的努力，這是上帝所喜悅和悅納的。

35.en: If thy brother. A brother, a stranger, or a sojourner in need was to be relieved. One who was comfortably situated must not take usury from a poor brother, nor make a profit on food sold to him (see on Ex. 22:25). Thus again is shown God’s care for the poor. God had delivered Israel from Egypt and was about to take them into the land of Canaan. As they had been the recipients of so much kindness, God wanted them to be kind to the unfortunate (see Matt. 10:8). Only thus could they receive God’s approval.
35.zh:
你的弟兄在你那裡若漸漸貧窮，手中缺乏，你就要幫補他，使他與你同住，像外人和寄居的一樣。

一遭遇困難的弟兄，外人或寄居者應該得到幫助。處境好的人不可向窮弟兄收取高利，也不可在賣給他的食物時賺錢（見出22:25註釋）。這再次顯明上帝對窮人的關愛。上帝把以色列人從埃及救出來，並將帶他們進入迦南。他們既領受了那麼多的福惠，上帝就要他們對不幸的人表顯仁慈（見太10:8）。只有這樣，他們才能得到上帝的悅納。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》186。
